name: Bonfire [✓]
description:
Adds multi-user profile switching to Jellyfin. A single account can have up to five isolated profiles — each with its own watch history, parental controls, and library access.  
  
Universal Repo 
Source: https://ahouseofbards.github.io/Bonfire-JellyProfiles/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/AHouseOfBards/Bonfire-JellyProfiles
overview: Multi-user profile switching for Jellyfin.

versions.changelog:
**Fixed**

- On 2019 LG TVs (webOS 4.5), Bonfire did not start at all. [#34]
- With "Ask who's watching on startup" off, there was no Switch Profile button and no way to switch.
- After signing out of the iOS app, the previous account's profile stayed on the sign-in screen and carried over to the next account.
- On iPad, your own profiles could appear as a linked Bonfire, and Manage Profiles asked you to open yourself first.
- The profile picture in the header was drawn zoomed in and blurry.

**Fixed**

- Security: any account could run script in an administrator's browser through the Bonfire settings page. Please update.
- Security: a PIN typed into a TV or app sign-in screen could be guessed with no limit.
- Security: someone using a profile in a browser could take over the main account behind it.
- On Android TV, Roku and other TV apps, choosing a profile and entering its PIN was refused.
- A profile limited to one TV could be missing from that TV's sign-in screen.
- Skipping Quick Connect on known TVs also removed it for other people with the same TV model.
- Signing in on a TV could occasionally fail with a server error.
- Creating a profile could fail with "The supplied value is invalid". [#33]
- The profile picker ran off the bottom of the screen on a TV. [#31]
- A profile kept its old rating after its account's rating was lowered.
- Clearing your PIN, or using the emergency disable code, could stop your password working.
- An account with a PIN could not change its Jellyfin password.
- Creating two profiles at once could go over the profile limit.
- The Signed-in devices list in the dashboard could fail to load.
- The create form showed only four libraries at a time.

**Changed**

- A profile keeps every restriction set on its account, such as remote access, schedules and bitrate.
- Profiles in another household's Bonfire need a PIN, unless their owner allows switching on the home network.
- Hidden Bonfire profiles can no longer be opened.
- Removing someone from your Bonfire changes its code, so they cannot rejoin with the old one.
- Reopening the app keeps the profile you were using. Going back to your main profile asks for its PIN.
- Manage Profiles needs your main profile open.

**Added**

- Thirty starter avatars to pick from, on by default. Turn them off in Dashboard -> Bonfire -> Avatar Library. [#32]
- Picture quality for profile pictures and avatars: Dashboard -> Bonfire -> Picture quality.
- A New code button for your Bonfire.
- A loader for the Samsung Tizen app, so Bonfire updates reach the TV without rebuilding the app. [#16]

**Fixed**

- Giving a profile a new library in Dashboard -> Users was undone the next time anyone entered that profile. Grants made there are now kept. To take a library away from a profile, edit the profile. [#30]
- Turning on "Skip Quick Connect on known devices" took Quick Connect away from apps that already have a password screen. It now applies only to Android TV, which is the one that needs it.

**Added**

- Profiles can appear on the sign-in screens of Jellyfin for Roku, Swiftfin, Findroid and Wholphin, the same as Android TV. Turn off automatic sign in on the app, or it goes straight into the last account.
- Apps that have no user list of their own can enter a profile by typing the profile's name and its PIN.

**Changed**

- The README is shorter. Library artwork, Bonfire sharing and known limitations now have their own pages under docs/.

**Added**

- Profiles can now appear on the sign-in screen of apps that never load the web client, such as Android TV, and be opened with their PIN. New settings under Dashboard -> Bonfire -> TVs & Apps, all off until you turn them on.
- On those screens a profile shows the name you gave it, not the full account name.
- An account that owns profiles can sign in with its PIN as well as its password.
- Apps can be sent straight to the password field instead of a Quick Connect code.
- "Who's watching?" on startup can be set per device instead of everywhere at once.

**Works on Jellyfin 12.0.** The same build serves 10.11 and 12.0 — there is nothing extra to install.

**Fixed**

- On Jellyfin 12.0 the Switch Profile button was missing from the header. Its default layout keeps the old header in the page but hides it, and Bonfire was adding the button there.
- In the profile form, text boxes would not take a click and dropdowns would not open — the page jumped to the top instead. Jellyfin's account menu was being left open, and its focus handling and Bonfire's fought each other.
- The Switch Profile button could appear beside the wrong icon at the wrong size, then move a second or two later. It now appears once, beside your account icon.
- Importing avatars from a folder failed on Jellyfin 12.0, and on any server where an administrator had turned legacy authorization off.
- The Bonfire section on your profile page sat against the left edge while the rest of the page was centred.
- The rename and merge buttons in the device list were unstyled, and drew as empty boxes on televisions without an emoji font.

**Changed**

- Bonfire follows your theme's accent colour on Jellyfin 12.0, which publishes that colour under a new name.

**Fixed**

- Switching to someone's main profile wiped that person's library access, and their sub-profiles' access with it. If this has happened to you, re-tick their libraries in Jellyfin's user settings after updating. [#27]
- Switching into an administrator's account quietly removed their admin rights and hid them from the login screen. [#27]
- Restricting a profile to specific devices could lock it out of every device, including the ones you picked. [#16]
- On a TV, picking a profile changed the name at the top but left you in your main account — same libraries, same Continue Watching, same Next Up. [#16]
- On a TV, moving off the first profile jumped straight to Manage Profiles and no other profile could be reached. [#16]
- On a TV the profile cards had no size and the focus outline never appeared, so nothing looked selectable. Save could also sit below the bottom of the profile form with no way to reach it on a remote. [#16]
- The profile switcher said you were signed in as your main profile even while a sub-profile was in use.
- A profile, device or Bonfire group you had just saved could silently not be there.
- Anything added while the plugin's settings page was open was undone when an administrator pressed Save.
- One computer could appear several times in the device list, and devices that sent no name all read as "Unknown Device".
- Forgetting a profile's only allowed device silently made that profile available everywhere. It is refused now, and says which profiles are in the way.
- "Try again in 15 minutes" after too many wrong PINs. It now tells you the wait it is actually enforcing, which is usually far less.
- Device "last seen" dates reset every time Jellyfin restarted, and the device list never dropped hardware nobody uses any more.
- A language could stop loading until Jellyfin was restarted, dropping everyone back to English.
- Switching profiles on a light theme flashed a black screen, and a switch that went wrong left the screen blank for four seconds.
- The profile screen re-downloaded every profile picture on every page load. Your browser keeps them now.

**Added**

- Bonfire knows when it is on a television, and makes the profile pictures, text and focus outline large enough to use from across a room.
- Rename a device, or tell Bonfire that two entries are the same machine. "Tidy up duplicates" folds together the several devices one browser makes — a profile allowed on any of them stays allowed.
- A list of everyone signed in, with the household each profile belongs to, and a way to sign one device out.
- Export and import the plugin's configuration, so there is a copy of your profiles and PINs somewhere other than one file.
- The audit log can be filtered by name and date, and downloaded.
- Polish, contributed by danis101. [#26]
- TROUBLESHOOTING.md, which answers the most common report first: Bonfire does not edit index.html by default, so a file with no plugin tags in it is a healthy install.

**Changed**

- The Switch Profile button now sits next to your account icon in the header, instead of at the end of the row.
- The interface reads correctly on light Jellyfin themes, where separators and muted text used to be invisible.
- Bonfire does far less work in the background — most noticeable on a TV, and it steps back further while something is playing.
- The "restart to finish updating" notice now names the version running and the version waiting, so you can tell whether your restart worked. [#25]

**New**

- Bonfire no longer edits Jellyfin's `index.html`. The client script is added to the page as it is served, so there is nothing to re-apply after a Jellyfin update and no file permissions to grant. Patching the file stays available as a legacy option under **Advanced → Client script**. (#17, #11, #3)
- The switcher follows your theme's accent colour instead of always drawing Jellyfin blue.
- Profile screens use the whole window on a desktop instead of one phone-width column.
- The picker shows which profile you are currently watching as.

**Fixed**

- On Android, picking a profile could bring the picker straight back, over and over, and a PIN-protected profile could drop you at the account login.
- Picking a profile showed nothing at all for the second or two it takes, so the tap read as missed. The profile you picked now shows a spinner, and the screen no longer goes black while it loads.
- Opening a profile took several seconds and could drop you back on a screen you had already left.
- Bonfire rewrote `index.html` on startup even when set never to touch it.
- The settings page reported the client script as installed whenever the plugin was loaded at all, including on servers where nothing was reaching the page.
- Add Profile was missing from the Manage Profiles screen.
- Library names were cut off to "3D Movi…" when choosing artwork.
- **Upload avatars** and **Upload a folder** were unstyled text instead of buttons.
- "PIN Protected" showed in red and "No PIN" in green — the wrong way round.
- The audit log ran the time into the address as "12:09:28 PMIP".

**Changed**

- The plugin is called **Bonfire** in the Jellyfin sidebar.
- Plugin settings are split into tabs — General, Avatars, Accounts, Activity and Advanced — instead of one page five screens tall.
- Switcher Style and Your Bonfire move out of the profile grid into their own **Settings** screen. Bonfire Grouping is now called Your Bonfire.
- Add Profile appears on Manage Profiles only. The "Who's watching?" screen is people to pick from.
- Setting a profile picture is one panel rather than six controls. The paste-a-URL box is gone: a linked picture could not be cropped, was never stored on your server, and disappeared without warning when the link died.
- Libraries and their artwork are one list, with the artwork controls behind a switch.
- Delete is no longer as prominent as Save.

**New**

- Library artwork can be set per profile. Jellyfin builds a library tile from the items inside it, so a Kids profile could see a poster from a film it cannot open; each profile can now be given its own picture for a library, or none at all. (#19)
- Administrators can set the switcher defaults for the whole server, under Dashboard → Plugins → Bonfire. Anyone who has already chosen keeps their own setting. (#14)
- Avatars can be uploaded several at a time, or a whole folder at once. Administrators with a prepared set already on the server can point at its folder and import it. (#14)
- The profile picker has a Cancel button when you opened it yourself, so you can go back to what you were watching.

**Fixed**

- Switching a profile failed with "Invalid username or password" on Jellyfin 10.11.11, and signed the master account out. (#15)
- On Samsung Tizen, picking a profile changed the avatar but left you in the original account. (#15, #16)
- On a TV, the remote could steer the Jellyfin page hidden behind the Bonfire screen. (#16)
- The TV Back button raised Samsung’s "exit application?" prompt behind the Bonfire screen. Back now steps back one screen instead. (#15)
- "Switch Profile" now appears on the Settings page, not only in the header dropdown. (#14)
- Profile pictures could be zoomed but not dragged.
- Save and Cancel are scrolled into view when a remote reaches them, so long profile forms no longer look frozen. (#15)
- Pictures now load in clients that bundle their own web client, such as Samsung Tizen.
- A missing script tag in index.html now says which of the three causes it is. (#17)

**Changed**

- The emergency disable link appears only once an administrator has set a code.
- Error messages, hints and warnings cut down throughout.

First stable release of the 1.3 line, consolidating the 1.2.x pre-releases. ■ NEW — Tag-based content filtering. Each sub-profile can block or allow content by Jellyfin tag (for example "adults", "teens", "kids"), alongside the existing parental rating limit. Tags are inherited, so tagging a series or a whole library applies to everything inside it, and enforcement happens server-side — meaning it holds on every client, including ones that cannot show the profile switcher at all. Blocked tags are additive with the master account's, and an allow-list can only narrow the master's, so a sub-profile can never see more than its parent. ■ NEW — Reorganised profile editor. Creating and editing a profile is now grouped into four titled sections: Profile (name, colour, picture), Security (PIN, LAN bypass, auto-lock), Libraries, and Content & Device Restrictions. Previously every field sat in one flat list in the order features had been added. Sections are plain blocks rather than collapsible panels so D-pad focus order on TV stays predictable, and the layout adapts to phone widths. ■ NEW — The settings page now lists master accounts with their sub-profiles nested underneath, instead of two separate tables. ■ SECURITY — Fixed a stored cross-site scripting flaw in profile avatar images and colours. Because Bonfire groups render profiles from linked households on each other's switcher screens, a crafted value could run script in another user's browser and steal their session token. Values are now validated on the server and escaped on render. ■ SECURITY — Profile PINs are now stored as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes rather than unsalted SHA-256, under which a 4-8 digit PIN was recoverable almost instantly from the configuration file. Existing PINs keep working and are upgraded automatically the next time they are entered. ■ SECURITY — An account with no PIN can no longer be switched into from a shared Bonfire, and the local-network PIN bypass no longer applies when stepping into another household's account. Also removed an open redirect on the profile image endpoint. ■ FIX — The dashboard's client-script warnings are now accurate. They re-check index.html on every page load rather than reporting server-startup state, a "Re-check Now" button re-runs the injection without a Jellyfin restart, and the message names the specific cause — including whether Jellyfin can write the file at all. The advisory notice can be dismissed on installs where the file is not writable without elevating. ■ FIX — Permission-fix commands are generated for the account Jellyfin actually runs as, rather than covering every possibility at once. ■ FIX — Editing a profile no longer erases device whitelist entries for devices that are switched off, and the device picker is correctly scoped to your own household. ■ FIX — A saved PIN no longer displays as "No PIN" on your own network, and profile changes appear immediately instead of requiring a page reload. ■ PERFORMANCE — Profile switching no longer rewrites the entire audit log on the request, the client script is served with revalidation so browsers pick up updates on their own, and a listener leak that made the interface progressively less responsive over a session has been fixed.

⚠️ BETA RELEASE — not a finished release; please report issues on GitHub. ▸ Settings page: master accounts and sub-profiles were listed as two separate tables, so working out which profiles belonged to which account meant reading the "Master Account" column on every row. There is now a single list of master accounts, each with its sub-profiles collapsed underneath it behind a "2 sub-profiles" toggle. PIN status and Reset PIN are available at both levels as before. Any sub-profile whose master account no longer exists — normally the residue of a partially failed deletion — is listed separately under "Unlinked sub-profiles" rather than disappearing, so it can still be found and managed. ▸ The permission-fix commands are now generated for the account Jellyfin is actually running as, and the page states which account that is. Previously they had to cover every possibility at once: on Windows, Jellyfin runs either as a service (NT AUTHORITY\NetworkService) or as the signed-in user when installed as a tray/desktop app, so the icacls command granted Modify to ALL local users in order to work in both cases. It now grants access to exactly one account — the real one — which is both less to type and a considerably narrower permission on a file inside Program Files. ▸ The same applies to the Linux and Docker chown commands, which previously assumed the service account was named "jellyfin". That is the convention but not a guarantee, and the commands silently did nothing useful when it was not. If the account cannot be determined, the page falls back to the previous broader commands, so nothing is lost on unusual setups.

New: Tag-based content filtering for sub-profiles. Each profile can now block or allow content by Jellyfin tag (e.g. 'adults', 'teens', 'kids'), matching Jellyfin's own parental-control tag feature. Tags are inherited, so tagging a series or an entire library applies to everything inside it, and enforcement is server-side so it holds on every client. Blocked tags are additive with the master account's and an allow-list can only narrow the master's, so a sub-profile can never see more than its parent. Security: fixed a stored XSS in profile avatar images and colours — these are rendered on other households' switcher screens via Bonfire groups, so a crafted value could steal another user's session token; values are now validated server-side and escaped on render. Security: profile PINs are now stored as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes instead of unsalted SHA-256 (a 4-8 digit PIN was trivially recoverable from the config file); existing PINs keep working and upgrade automatically on next entry. Security: an account with no PIN can no longer be switched into from a shared Bonfire, and the LAN PIN bypass no longer applies across accounts. Security: removed an open redirect on the profile image endpoint. Fix: the client-script injection now verifies the script is actually present before reporting success — previously an index.html without the expected anchors reported success while the switcher silently never loaded, and the dashboard's failure banner could never appear. Fix: index.html is now written atomically so an interrupted write cannot corrupt the Jellyfin web client. Fix: audit log entries no longer reverse order when trimmed.

Fix: Plugin now loads correctly on Jellyfin 10.11.5. The previous release was compiled against 10.11.6, which caused a loader-level assembly version mismatch (FileNotFoundException on MediaBrowser.Common/Controller/Model) on servers running 10.11.5. Compile target downgraded to 10.11.5 — the plugin remains fully compatible with 10.11.6 and later patch releases.
Release 1.1.0: Codebase cleanup, optimization, documentation updates, and developer API reference alignment.
Initial release.

versions.changelog:
This update brings together 2.0.10.0 and 2.0.11.0 from the beta channel.

If you use the Live TV allow-list behind a reverse proxy: add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings. Without that, every request through the proxy counts as coming from the proxy, and if its address is on your list, everyone gets in. The help text now says so.

Fixed: with Live TV set up on two or more providers, the guide never used your providers' XMLTV files. They were combined into one file that could not be read past the first provider, so the guide always fell back to the simpler per-channel listings and lost categories, ratings and the other details XMLTV carries. Each provider's file is now read on its own. If one provider's file is missing or broken, only that provider's channels fall back, and the others keep their full guide (found and fixed by dillardblom).

Fixed: when two providers used the same guide id for different channels, one of them got no guide, or showed the other provider's programmes. Guide ids are now matched per provider (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: when your provider's XMLTV guide came through cut off part way, building the guide never finished. Each request for the EPG URL kept one CPU core busy until Jellyfin gave up, and the guide stayed empty. A broken file now falls back to fetching the guide per channel, as it already did when the file was missing, and no programme is listed twice (by dillardblom).

Fixed: with Dispatcharr mode on, every sync worker logged in to Dispatcharr at the same time when a sync started. Dispatcharr's login limit refused most of them, and those workers fell back to the Xtream API for the first minutes. There is now one login shared by all of them, and it waits its turn like every other request (reported by dillardblom).

This update brings together 2.0.2.0 to 2.0.9.0 from the beta channel.

If you use Live TV with the Native Tuner only, open the Live TV tab after updating and turn off the new "Publish Playlists" switch. It stays on for anyone who already had Live TV enabled, so an M3U tuner or TiviMate setup keeps working, but the native tuner does not need it.

Fixed: Request Delay now limits how fast the plugin talks to your provider in total. Each parallel worker used to apply it separately, so with Sync Parallelism at 10 and the default of 50 ms up to 200 requests a second could go out, enough for some providers to block your IP. It is now one shared gap per provider: 50 ms means at most 20 a second. When the provider says it is getting too many requests, every request to it waits. A first sync of a large library takes longer as a result; if your provider allows more, lower Request Delay. Setting it to 0 is no longer saved as 50 (reported by dillardblom).

Fixed: a single unreadable value from your provider, such as an empty value where a number belongs, no longer makes content disappear. It could blank a series' title, plot and TMDB id, drop every episode of a series, or make a whole category fail to sync. Such values are now ignored or read as 0, and an item whose ID cannot be read is skipped with a warning while the rest syncs normally (reported by foXaCe).

Fixed: changing Folder Mode, or moving a category to another folder, no longer leaves every moved item in your library twice. The old copies are removed even beyond the orphan safety limit, as long as the item only moved to another category folder; anything that actually disappeared is still protected by the limit. Moved items lose their watched status, because Jellyfin sees a new folder as a new item (reported in andreadegiovine's fork).

Fixed: when orphan cleanup removes a movie or series, the NFO and poster the plugin wrote are removed with it, so the folder no longer stays behind. Files you added yourself, such as subtitles or your own NFO, are kept, and so is the folder (idea from andreadegiovine).

Fixed: with "Group movies with the same TMDB id" on, a film whose request the provider missed no longer ends up in a folder of its own. It is held back and picked up on the next sync. Films already split this way stay split; to fix them, use Delete Movies Library in the Danger Zone and sync again (reported by andreadegiovine).

New: with "Fallback to Year-Free Lookup" on, an unmatched movie is also searched with the year of the provider's release date and with its original title, which helps when the title carries the wrong year or is in another language. A search without a year is checked against the release date, so it cannot pick a remake. A match found by the year-free retry is now remembered for later syncs, for movies and series. Movies already in your library keep their folders (idea from philx17).

New: "Publish Playlists" on the Live TV tab. The M3U and Catch-up M3U URLs contain your Xtream username and password and can be reached without a Jellyfin login. They are now only served while this switch is on, and it is off when you enable Live TV from now on. The EPG URL and channel logos are not affected (proposed by dillardblom).

New: "Restrict These URLs To" limits the Live TV URLs to the addresses you list, one per line. Leave it empty for no restriction. If you use it, include 127.0.0.1 and ::1, since Jellyfin fetches channel logos itself, and behind a reverse proxy add the proxy to Known Proxies in Jellyfin's networking settings first (written by dillardblom).

Fixed: a Live TV category, channel or logo address with & in it no longer shows as & or breaks (reported by TheBazeman).

Categories load their items again on Jellyfin 12 (#117).

Jellyfin 12 stops accepting the legacy `X-Emby-Token` request header. Two of the configuration page fetch sites still sent it: the Live TV category loader and the Series / VOD content loader. Both now send `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token=` instead, which Jellyfin 12's `CustomAuthentication` middleware expects. The Test connection button was never affected and still works as before. Two-line header swap in `config.js`, no server-side change.

versions.changelog: ⚠️ This plugin has moved to a new GUID. You won't see future updates on this entry. After updating, open the plugin catalog and install 'Xtream Library' (it will appear as a separate entry with the new GUID), then uninstall this plugin and restart Jellyfin. Provider settings, library folders, and channel selections carry over automatically. See https://github.com/firestaerter3/Jellyfin-Xtream-Library/issues/46 for context.

Fix legacy-config migration silently failing on upgrades from pre-v1.32 releases. The [Obsolete] attribute on the legacy single-provider fields caused .NET's XmlSerializer to skip them during deserialization, so the on-startup migration into Providers[0] never ran. After this fix the existing provider settings are picked up on first restart. Pairs with v1.33.1.0's Live TV credential-check fix.

Fix connection test crash when provider returns "N/A" for active_cons or max_connections: some Xtream providers send non-numeric strings for these user info fields, which now fall back to 0 instead of throwing a deserialization error (fixes #39).

Add regex removal patterns for STRM file names: new 'Regex Removal Patterns' config field (alongside the existing substring 'Custom Title Removal Terms') applies to file names only, leaving folders untouched so Jellyfin metadata providers keep [tmdbid-N] / [tvdbid-N] identification (closes #32).

Fix episode names showing raw filenames when NFO creation is enabled: episode NFOs now only contain stream details, letting Jellyfin metadata providers (TMDb/TVDb) supply proper episode names (fixes #23).

Fix series sync failure on providers that return empty strings or omit numeric fields (last_modified, rating, episode_run_time, category_id) in the get_series response — all series categories now deserialize correctly (fixes #27).
Fix HLS stream format causing transcoding on every channel; default stream format changed from HLS to MPEG-TS for direct streaming with no server CPU usage.
Fix 403 errors for providers that require no Xtream credentials (e.g. iptorrents VIP bundled IPTV): empty username/password fields no longer send username=&password= in API requests.
Normalize colons in folder names for cross-platform compatibility: titles like '21 Paradise: Verkaufte Lust' now produce folders named '21 Paradise - Verkaufte Lust' (fixes #20).
Add year-free metadata lookup fallback option for providers with incorrect years in stream names.
Log stream URL and HTTP error when native tuner playback fails; fix year parsing for dash-suffix movie titles (e.g. 'Movie - 2025' now correctly splits into <title> and <year>)
Strip embedded series name, season and episode number from episode titles when providers include them (e.g. 'Breaking Bad - S01E01 - Pilot' no longer produces doubled filenames)
Write provider IDs to NFO files: movie NFOs now include <uniqueid type="tmdb"> and series folders get a tvshow.nfo, preventing repeated metadata lookups on every library scan (fixes #12, fixes #13)

name: Live-TV Control Center [✓✓]
description:

versions.changelog:
- Administrators can now copy central groups into their own personal collection when switching back to personal mode, or import them later. Both management screens require an explicit copy/skip choice on mode switch. Existing personal groups take precedence when IDs match; central groups and other users' personal groups remain untouched. Custom group images are copied with newly imported groups.
- Require administrators to explicitly choose whether to copy their personal groups when switching to central management. The no-copy choice preserves personal groups for later use, and both the web dialog and plugin dashboard offer a later import. Reject an ambiguous mode-switch request instead of silently showing an empty central group list.

- Support Wholphin in the native Live TV guide: select a group or **All channels** directly in its compatible Control Center folders, then open **Live TV → TV Guide**. Group selection applies only to the authenticated user's device, respects current group/channel permissions, and restores the full guide on reset. Wholphin does not support an automatic guide jump.
- Add administrator switches for the official Jellyfin Android TV / Fire TV app and Wholphin. A sole eligible TV is selected automatically; with several TVs, the last available choice is remembered per user. Disabled or disconnected devices cannot receive playback or guide changes.
- Add recognizable artwork to the Control Center home tile, guide actions, confirmation and fallback folders. **All channels** has its own EPG-reset image; created groups have a distinct group image. Personal and shared groups can use custom PNG, JPEG or WebP images up to 5 MiB, with preview and reset controls and permission checks.
- Add recording controls to the grouped web EPG. Users with Jellyfin's Live TV management permission can schedule, edit and cancel single-program or series timers, including padding and series options; recording errors remain visible in the dialog.
- Restore reliable loading of the independent web EPG behind reverse proxies that cached its old script URL. Preserve original channel logos, official Android TV / Fire TV behavior, channel playback and the existing plugin identity and settings.

- Selecting a group in the official Android TV / Fire TV app immediately applies that group's native guide scope and opens the ordinary Live TV view. The separate Native TV guide action remains available to retry.
- Hide direct grouped-channel media tiles from that authenticated TV response while keeping the native guide action and browsable program-list fallback. Internal channel items and playlists remain unchanged.
- Retain per-user/device validation, group access checks and safe behavior when navigation is unavailable. The original app may still require selecting TV Guide after opening Live TV; a direct timeline deep link is not exposed by the stock client.

- Organize Live TV channels in ordered personal groups independent of IPTV-provider categories, or use administrator-managed shared groups with per-group user access.
- Show one selected group's original channels in Jellyfin's native Android TV / Fire TV timeline. Select the group on the TV or from the web/mobile page; the web page can also apply the deduplicated union of all visible groups. Reset to all ordinarily permitted channels at any time. Selections are per user and TV device.
- Browse an independent web EPG with a channel/program timeline, now/next/later programs, channel cards, day/time navigation and zoom. Save visible/default groups and view preferences; use the interface in English or German.
- Use the web or phone guide as a remote for the official Jellyfin Android TV / Fire TV app: discover a compatible TV, remember the target, and start or switch live channels while the guide stays open.
- Apply optional central channel-access rules to selected users, including children's accounts. Restrictions cover the plugin and ordinary Jellyfin Live TV, direct playback, playlists and associated recordings while preserving Jellyfin permissions.
- Browse grouped channel and daily program folders in supported native apps; optionally mirror groups as playlists for other clients.
- Integrate the web interface through File Transformation, optionally add a Plugin Pages menu shortcut, customize the display name and hide the original Live TV home tile when the groups entry is available.
- Support Jellyfin 12.0 or later in the Jellyfin 12 series (12.1 confirmed). Keep the existing plugin ID, channel identity and stored settings for upgrades from Live-TV Groups. Native guide navigation may require one additional TV Guide selection; no virtual channels or custom TV client are used.

### 0.2.0.1
Revert the 0.2.0.0 web UI takeover — the injected `/jellyfish/ui/home.js` script triggered a browser HTTP Basic auth prompt on the Jellyfin login page and locked users out of the web client.
- Removes the FileTransformation registration and all injected ES modules.

v0.2.0.0

Add a full web UI takeover that ports the Jellyfish mobile home page to jellyfin-web.

- Inject custom ES modules into Jellyfin's web client via `jellyfin-plugin-file-transformation`.
- Render a hero carousel, Jellyseerr discovery rails (trending, popular, watchlist, watch providers, genre sliders, 5 mood rails, history-seeded recommendations), Radarr/Sonarr upcoming rails, and native Jellyfin rails (continue, next up, latest, per-library).
- Add a Seerr request modal with season selector (POSTs to `/jellyfish/jellyseerr/request`).
- Hide native Jellyfin home sections except the library shortcuts row.
- Style matches the Flutter mobile app (Fraunces / Fira Code / Inter, dark palette, pill chips).
- Includes a deploy-local fix: stop the container before swapping the plugin directory to avoid Jellyfin marking the plugin as missing.

Requires `jellyfin-plugin-file-transformation` to be installed on the target Jellyfin server (manifest: https://www.iamparadox.dev/jellyfin/plugins/manifest.json).

Add Jellyseerr `movie/{id}/similar` and `tv/{id}/similar` passthroughs so the "Because you watched…" rail can resolve.
- Both forward the full incoming query string (page, language, …).

Forward full query string on Jellyseerr discover passthroughs.
- `discover/movies`, `discover/tv`, `discover/watchlist` now forward every query param (sortBy, voteCountGte, voteAverageGte, genre, watchRegion, watchProviders, …) instead of only `page`.
- Remove `GET /jellyfish/jellyseerr/config`: exposing the admin X-Api-Key to authenticated clients is no longer needed now that the passthrough is transparent.

Add `GET /jellyfish/jellyseerr/config` — returns the configured Jellyseerr URL and admin API key to authenticated callers so the mobile client can hit `/api/v1/discover/...` directly with the full TMDB query surface (sortBy, voteCountGte, voteAverageGte, …). 503 when the plugin isn't configured.

Add Jellyseerr proxy endpoints to eliminate client 404s:
- `GET /jellyfish/jellyseerr/watchproviders/movies` (optional `?watchRegion=`)

## 兼容性说明

为了避免升级 Jellyfin 12 后可能与 Jellyfin 10.11 不兼容的情况，保留此版本作为 Jellyfin 10.11 的最后一个版本。

后续插件将不再考虑 Jellyfin 10.11 的兼容性，若出现不兼容情况，可以下载此版本。

## 新功能与改进

- 增加按用户管理 Bangumi 授权，以及 NSFW 播放记录的私密上报选项。
- 增加缺失 Bangumi ID 的补全工具和 `bangumi.ini` 媒体库管理功能，改进批量选择及刷新反馈。
- 增加动画搜索偏好和优先使用原始标题搜索的配置，支持自定义 Bangumi 网站地址。
- 引入 Anitomy 剧集解析器，改进文件名、集数和多季度识别。
- 增强音乐元数据与播放记录同步，调整插件设置页面。

## 问题修复

- 修复 Bangumi 图片地址和搜索结果处理问题。
- 修复剧集与季度未读取 `bangumi.ini`、未知季度和重复剧集扫描中的特别篇识别问题。
- 修复音乐刮削中的元数据丢失及艺人类型筛选问题。
- 修复 infobox 解析死循环及重复字段处理。
- 改进异步请求、取消操作、评分刷新和播放状态缓存处理。

**完整更新记录**：https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/compare/1.7.6...1.7.7

## New Features 增加了重复剧集检测小工具，用于替换字幕组、发布 V2 版时自动清理旧版本 ## What's Changed * fix: handle null and empty ChineseName correctly by @chu-shen in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/232 * fix: Emby plugin support for macOS ARM and .NET 6 runtime by @nihs903222 in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/233 * fix: implement IHasSupportedExternalIdentifiers for Emby by @sjtuross in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/236 * 修复Subject的PersonInfos或Characters拉取失败导致整个Subject的元数据拉取失败的问题 by @HydrogensaysHDT in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/238 ## New Contributors * @nihs903222 made their first contribution in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/233 * @sjtuross made their first contribution in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/236 * @HydrogensaysHDT made their first contribution in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/238 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/compare/1.7.5...1.7.6

## What's Changed
* 支持人物搜索
* 为 Emby 添加 bangumi.ini 支持 by @luoboQAQ in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/224
* 优化 markdown 换行转换，对于不支持 markdown 显示的第三方播放器更友好
* 修复元数据中 `Bangumi ID` 显示为 `Bangumi 专辑 ID` 的问题
* 修复插件配置目录不存在导致的登录失败 #218
* 添加了插件 logo 图（改自 https://www.pixiv.net/artworks/4455303 ）

## New Contributors
* @luoboQAQ made their first contribution in https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/pull/224

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/kookxiang/jellyfin-plugin-bangumi/compare/1.7.4...1.7.5

  breakdown in the results table

versions.changelog:
AniLiberty STRM 3.0.0.0 — Jellyfin 12

### Changes

- Fixed intro and outro skips disappearing after repeated library updates.
- Corrected skip timings now apply to episodes already in your library.
- Temporary read errors no longer remove saved skip timings.

### Upgrade Notes

Restart Jellyfin after updating. No settings changes or library regeneration are required.

AniLiberty STRM 2.0.0.15 — Jellyfin 12

### Changes

- Added support for Jellyfin 12.
- Reduced unnecessary artwork downloads during library updates.
- Reduced background processing for intro and outro skipping.
- Fixed a problem that could remove generated library files when AniLiberty returned incomplete data.

### Upgrade Notes

Restart Jellyfin after updating. No settings changes or library regeneration are required.

## ✨ New Features

- **Issue a certificate now:** Request a new certificate before renewal is due, even when automatic management is disabled. Save your settings first; the button uses your saved staging/production and restart settings.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Issuance limits:** Manual requests retain the six-hour cooldown and certificate authority rate limits.

## ✨ New Features

- **Certificate issued date:** Show the certificate validity start date in your local time.
- **Repository link:** Open the GitHub repository from the top of the plugin configuration page.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Expired certificate status:** Resolved an issue where certificate status could remain outdated after expiration, including when automatic management was disabled.
- **Status messages:** Keep renewal errors visible and replace obsolete restart instructions.

## ✨ New Features

- **Certificate cleanup:** Retain replaced AutoCert certificates for five days after first observing them unused with the replacement active, then remove them at the next scheduled 12-hour check.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Protected certificates:** Keep the active production certificate, latest staging certificate, and externally supplied files. Cleanup waits for any pending restart.
- **Upgrade grace period:** Give existing old files a fresh five-day grace period when upgrading. Rollback to a deleted certificate is no longer available.
- **Stable release:** AutoCert 1.0.0.0 is now a regular release.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Duplicate status text:** Resolved an issue where Certificate Active appeared twice when activity and certificate status matched. Distinct progress and error messages remain visible.

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **Status after restart:** Resolved a stale restart message. Show Certificate Active when Jellyfin reports HTTPS listening, no restart is pending, certificate settings match, and the AutoCert PFX is valid.

## 🎨 Improvements

- **Error visibility:** Preserve staging messages and renewal failures.

## ✨ New Features

- **GoDaddy authentication:** Use a classic API key and secret alongside the existing GoDaddy PAT, Cloudflare, and DigitalOcean options.
- **HTTPS management:** DNS verification, automatic renewal, password-protected PFX creation, password rotation, Jellyfin HTTPS configuration updates, optional restart, and rollback.

versions.changelog: Fix: re-added missing Pocket ID preset and other small UI fixes

The hardened OIDC rewrite on Jellyfin 12. Hand-rolled OIDC flow with Trust-On-First-Use discovery-endpoint pinning and an SSRF-guarded, DNS-rebind-pinned HTTP client. Account identity keyed on the OIDC subject, in its own identity-map file (migrated out of the plugin config on upgrade). Fail-closed role-to-policy RBAC with a server-wide admission allowlist. OIDC Back-Channel Logout 1.0. Client-secret indirection (Client Secret File / ENV_VAR reference). Auto-managed SSO login button in Branding. Rewritten admin config page. Opt-in, per-provider verified-email account linking that never binds an administrator account. Username/email/display-name/email-verified now fall back to the userinfo endpoint when the ID token omits them. Token-validation failures surface a plain-language reason (expired cert, audience/issuer mismatch, clock drift, JWKS rotation) instead of a bare error. Fixed OIDC-authenticated sessions showing a blank IP in Jellyfin's activity log. Fixed the Manage Library Access checkbox not responding to clicks. No configuration migration required from 2.0.0.0. Renamed to SSO-OIDC-Authentication (was SSO-OIDC Authentication) so the install folder no longer mixes a space with a hyphen; your saved settings are unaffected.

BREAKING: requires Jellyfin 12.0 or newer will not load on 10.10/10.11 (stay on 1.0.7.x for those). Retargeted to .NET 10 and rebuilt against the Jellyfin 12.0 plugin API. Removed the vestigial IAuthenticationProvider.HasPassword override (dropped from the interface in 12.0). No functional changes to the OIDC login, RBAC, or Quick Connect flows.

versions.changelog: An **animated GIF background now also moves in the live preview in Firefox**. It only moved in Chrome, Edge and other Chromium-based browsers before; Firefox kept showing a single frame. The preview now plays the GIF in real time at its own speed, redrawn up to about 15 times a second (very fast GIFs skip frames in the preview to keep time). Covers you applied were never affected: they always animated. Browsers that cannot decode an image frame by frame (Safari, for example) still show a still preview, but the applied cover animates as usual.

A polish release for the editor, driven by a full review of the page. **Spacing is fixed**: since the guided-steps redesign some controls sat flush against each other (the Restore button touched the Type dropdown, *In context* touched Dimensions) while other gaps were twice as big. Every step now has one even rhythm, and dropdowns line up with the buttons beside them. **Errors are readable**: when the server refuses a request you now see why — your session expired, the file is too large, too many requests, or the server's own reason for refusing a design — in your own language, instead of *"Unexpected end of JSON input"*, and nothing is left stuck on "Applying…". **Fewer surprises**: Restore, deleting a template and batch apply now ask before they act (like Reset backup already did), batch apply says how many covers it will replace and can no longer be started twice, loading a template asks before replacing changes you have not applied, and the browser warns before you close the tab with unapplied work — only when the design really differs from what you last applied, saved or loaded. Undo and loading a template **keep your background image** on the preview instead of dropping it, and an animated GIF background keeps moving. Choosing a **Custom** size or **Animated GIF** now shows their settings straight away, and **Save this design** and **Apply to several targets** are no longer tucked away under Advanced. Custom sizes stay between 100 and 2048 pixels, which is what the server accepts. The editor now **works from the keyboard and with a screen reader**: select layers with Tab and Enter, move the selected layer with the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps; Alt, Ctrl and Meta combinations are left to the browser), and use the poster browser as a proper dialog that Esc closes and that keeps keyboard focus inside while you page through posters. Every icon button has a name. The poster browser follows **light themes** and the Jellyfin theme colours too. On narrow screens the layer **⋯** button works again. The title starts as the name of the target you pick, the Apply button says what it applies to (library, collection, playlist or Live TV), and switching the display language back to English no longer leaves Dutch or Spanish labels behind. Ctrl+Z now also undoes a slider or colour change, and is no longer intercepted on other dashboard pages. Existing designs and saved templates are unaffected and render exactly as before.

The live preview and the cover that actually gets applied now **agree on text effects**. A **shadow's softness** came out twice as wide on the applied cover as in the preview; it now matches, so a cover with a blurred text shadow looks slightly sharper than before once you apply it again. An **outline on semi-transparent text** used to stay fully solid on the cover however far you turned the opacity down; it now fades with the text, as the preview always showed, and outline corners are a little rounder. On **rotated text**, the cover turned the shadow along with the letters while the preview kept it falling the same way on screen; the cover now does what the preview shows. The preview itself had a few slips of its own: semi-transparent text with a shadow was drawn **slightly too dense**, the **in-context previews** (wide, square, poster) drew text, shadow and outline at full size so they spilled out of the little thumbnails, an **uploaded font** looked artificially bold when the weight was set to bold (the cover never was), and a **gradient from an old template** with fewer than two colour stops showed different colours in the editor, the preview and the cover. All three now show the same colours. Covers you have already applied are not changed until you apply them again. Fully opaque, unrotated text without a blurred shadow or an outline looks the same as before.

A **fix-up release for backups and the live preview**.
**Applying a cover a second time could be refused** with *"Could not back up the current cover"* on libraries that had no backup before 4.0.2.0. The backup was saved under one spelling of the library's id and looked for under another. Backups made by earlier versions are found again, so they keep working and the refusals stop.
**Covers made by this plugin are no longer saved as the "original".** The plugin now remembers the cover it applied last and never backs that up, nor anything in its own data folder. A backup is no longer made of a cover the plugin applied. If you applied covers with an earlier version before a target's first backup was taken (while trying the plugin out, for example), that backup may hold one of those test covers, and **Restore original cover** brings the test cover back instead of the real original. Covers applied by 4.0.2.0 are not recognised as plugin covers until you have applied once with this version.
The new **Reset backup** button next to Restore deletes a target's backup. It saves nothing itself: the next apply stores the cover the target shows at that moment as the new original, unless it is a cover the plugin applied. To fix a wrong backup, first put the cover you want to keep back on the library: upload it in Jellyfin (**Edit images** in the dashboard), or delete the poster and refresh metadata with *Replace existing images*. Then press **Reset backup**, then apply. This matters most if your old backup holds an early test cover, because your true original was overwritten before backups existed and has to come from you. Restores, backups and skipped backups are now written to the Jellyfin log.
In the editor, a **poster collage** background now shows in the live preview. It used to stay black until you pressed Show server render. An **animated GIF** background now moves in the preview instead of standing still, unless your system is set to reduce motion.

A **hardening and housekeeping** release — apart from the fixes below, nothing about how you design covers changes. Applied covers now go through **Jellyfin's own image handling**, the same path as uploading an image in the dashboard, so they are stored alongside the rest of your library artwork and, for covers applied or restored from this version on, **keep working even if the plugin's data folder is cleared** (covers applied by 4.0.1.0 and never re-applied still live in that folder); **Restore original cover** works exactly as before. If the current cover cannot be backed up first, applying is now **refused with a clear message** and the cover is left untouched, so the cover you had before you first used the plugin can always be restored (a cover you set in the dashboard after an earlier apply is replaced by the next apply, as with Jellyfin's own upload). A logo or icon layer scaled larger than **1.5× the canvas** now renders at most 1.5×, so old templates with huge logos render smaller. **Animated images are handled far more carefully**: the server only ever decodes the frames it actually needs (one for a still cover, at most 60 for an animated one). A long or high-resolution animated GIF is no longer turned away — the plugin simply uses as many of its frames as fit safely in memory — and only an image whose single frame is larger than 8192×8192 pixels is **refused at upload with a clear message**. **Ken Burns** covers no longer **stretch** a background whose shape differs from the cover, animated covers render faster, and a shrunk animated GIF keeps its blur and border in proportion. A single faulty text layer can no longer **blank out the whole cover** — it is skipped and everything else still renders. Size errors such as *"Dimensions too large"* are now shown as they are instead of a generic failure. Behind the scenes, the applied-cover folder no longer grows with every apply, applying to the same library or collection is now done one at a time so two applies can no longer overwrite each other, rapid repeated requests can no longer slip past the rate limits (rejected uploads now count toward the upload limit too), and saving a template while a batch apply runs is now safe. **TIFF uploads are no longer accepted** — browsers cannot draw TIFF in the editor, so they never previewed properly; convert to PNG or JPG. The background upload limit can now be changed with `MaxUploadSizeMb` in the plugin's configuration file (1–50 MB, default 5); values above about 28 MB may still be blocked earlier by the web server's own request-size limit.

Fixes the configuration page on Jellyfin 12, where **nothing worked**. Jellyfin 12 stopped accepting the older of its two ways of proving who you are, and the page was still using it — so every request it made was rejected before it reached the plugin. Libraries did not load, saved templates did not appear, the bundled fonts did not arrive, applying a cover did nothing, and opening the poster browser produced the cryptic message *"Failed to execute 'json' on 'Response': Unexpected end of JSON input"*, which was the rejection with no explanation attached. The page now identifies itself the same way the Jellyfin web client does, which works on Jellyfin 10.11 and 12 alike. **If you installed 4.0.0.0, update** — nothing was wrong with your settings or your covers, the page simply could not reach the server.

**Support for Jellyfin 12.** Jellyfin 12 moved to .NET 10 and changed its plugin ABI, so a plugin built for 10.11 cannot be built for both — this release is built against Jellyfin 12 and requires it. Nothing about designing or rendering covers has changed: your saved templates, applied covers and settings all carry over untouched. If you are **still on Jellyfin 10.11**, stay on **3.5.1.0** — your server will keep being offered that version and will not see this one, so nothing breaks by leaving it alone.

versions.changelog:
## Español

### 3.1.0 — Retención de respaldos, endurecimiento y nueva interfaz

**Novedades**
- Retención de respaldos: define cuántos días se conserva cada backup (0 = sin límite, valor por defecto) y cuántos de los más recientes se conservan siempre (5 por defecto). Solo se borran archivos con el nombre que genera el plugin; cualquier otro archivo de la carpeta no se toca. Se aplica tras cada backup, con la nueva tarea programada «PostgreSQL Backup Retention» (diaria, 03:00) y con el botón «Depurar respaldos ahora», que muestra una vista previa y pide confirmación. Funciona igual en Windows, Linux y macOS.
- Interfaz renovada con el mismo diseño que JellyTV: pantalla completa y responsive, selects y checkboxes propios, título con descripción y pestaña Mantenimiento reordenada (operaciones, respaldos con retención, tareas programadas). Los resultados y avisos salen como notificaciones abajo a la derecha: las operaciones en curso muestran un indicador y los éxitos desaparecen solos. VACUUM, respaldos, optimizaciones, reparación y migración piden confirmación con el mismo modal, que ya no se cierra al pulsar fuera. «Actualizar estadísticas» pasa a Health.
- Aviso en el log, en el estado y en la interfaz cuando hay copias obsoletas del plugin junto a la que está en ejecución (por ejemplo una carpeta antigua marcada como eliminada), que Jellyfin puede seguir cargando.

**Seguridad y fiabilidad**
- **Cambio de comportamiento:** `Search/Instant` ahora exige un usuario autenticado. Antes era anónimo y permitía listar `BaseItems` sin sesión.
- La consola SQL se ejecuta en una transacción de solo lectura con límites de tiempo y rechaza las comillas de dólar, que permitían ocultar una segunda sentencia.
- La caché de consultas invalida también las escrituras de `SaveChanges` y al confirmar transacciones; antes podía servir datos antiguos hasta 30 s.
- Guardar la configuración valida la conexión cuando PostgreSQL está activo, rechaza cadenas vacías, escribe `database.xml` de forma atómica (con copia `.bak`) y la API ya no devuelve la contraseña en claro.
- Los agregados `min/max(uuid)` se dan por creados solo tras un intento exitoso; `pg_dump` y `psql` se terminan al cancelar y un volcado fallido ya no deja un `.sql` parcial.
- Las fechas se convierten a UTC al leer y escribir, y la variable `JELLYFIN_PG_DISABLE_QUERY_CACHE=1` permite descartar la caché al diagnosticar.

Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 o posterior y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.1.0 — Backup retention, hardening, and a new interface

**What's new**
- Backup retention: choose how many days each backup is kept (0 = keep forever, the default) and how many of the newest backups are always kept (5 by default). Only files named the way the plugin names them are deleted; any other file in the folder is left alone. It runs after every backup, through the new «PostgreSQL Backup Retention» scheduled task (daily, 03:00), and with the «Prune backups now» button, which shows a preview and asks for confirmation. It behaves the same on Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- Redesigned interface matching JellyTV: full-width and responsive, custom selects and checkboxes, a page title with description, and a reordered Maintenance tab (operations, backups with retention, scheduled tasks). Results and alerts appear as notifications at the bottom right: running operations show an indicator and successes dismiss themselves. VACUUM, backups, optimizations, repair, and migration ask for confirmation with the same modal, which no longer closes when you click outside. «Refresh statistics» moves to Health.
- A warning in the log, the status endpoint, and the interface when stale copies of the plugin sit next to the running one (for example an old folder marked as deleted) that Jellyfin may still load.

**Security and reliability**
- **Behavior change:** `Search/Instant` now requires a signed-in user. It used to be anonymous and could list `BaseItems` without a session.
- The SQL console runs in a read-only transaction with time limits and rejects dollar quoting, which could hide a second statement.
- The query cache also invalidates `SaveChanges` writes and transaction commits; it could previously serve stale data for up to 30 s.
- Saving the configuration validates the connection when PostgreSQL is active, rejects empty strings, writes `database.xml` atomically (with a `.bak` copy), and the API no longer returns the password in clear text.
- The `min/max(uuid)` aggregates are marked as created only after a successful attempt; `pg_dump` and `psql` are terminated on cancel and a failed dump no longer leaves a partial `.sql`.
- Dates are converted to UTC on read and write, and `JELLYFIN_PG_DISABLE_QUERY_CACHE=1` lets you rule out the cache when diagnosing.

Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 or newer, and .NET 10.

## Español

### 3.0.4 — Fechas, búsqueda, guardado y migración

- Corrige el cierre de Jellyfin Android TV al abrir bibliotecas: el caché de consultas descartaba `DateTimeKind.Utc` al bufferizar y el cliente recibía fechas sin zona horaria, que sustituía por su valor mínimo y hacían fallar la conversión. Las columnas de fecha se bufferizan como UTC y el lector restaura el `Kind` como segunda barrera.
- Nueva migración que normaliza fechas no finitas o mínimas ya guardadas en `BaseItems`, y normalización de los centinelas `DateTime` y `DateTimeOffset` antes de escribir.
- La búsqueda deja de distinguir mayúsculas y minúsculas e incluye título visible, título original y título para ordenar, con índice trigram sobre `SortName`.
- Corrige el error 500 al abrir la ficha de un artista o persona: las filas duplicadas se resuelven con una actualización sin cambios sobre la clave primaria en lugar de `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, que informaba 0 filas y EF Core trataba como conflicto de concurrencia.
- Corrige la migración SQLite → PostgreSQL: se conserva el historial de rutinas de código ya aplicadas, identificadas por el nombre de la migración. Sin él, Jellyfin volvía a ejecutar rutinas que esperan `library.db` y el arranque fallaba con `no such table: TypedBaseItems` (#9).
- El proveedor fija `QuerySplittingBehavior` en `SingleQuery`, igual que el proveedor SQLite, y deja de llenar el log con `MultipleCollectionIncludeWarning`.

Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 o posterior y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.0.4 — Dates, search, saving, and migration

- Fixes Jellyfin Android TV crashing when a library is opened: the query cache dropped `DateTimeKind.Utc` while buffering, so the client received dates without a time zone, replaced them with its minimum value, and failed converting it. Date columns are buffered as UTC and the reader restores the `Kind` as a second safeguard.
- New migration that normalizes non-finite or minimum dates already stored in `BaseItems`, plus normalization of `DateTime` and `DateTimeOffset` sentinels before writing.
- Search is no longer case-sensitive and now covers display, original, and sort titles, with a trigram index on `SortName`.
- Fixes the 500 returned when opening an artist or person page: duplicate rows are resolved with a no-op update on the primary key instead of `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, which reported zero affected rows and EF Core treated as a concurrency conflict.
- Fixes the SQLite → PostgreSQL migration: the history of code migrations already applied is preserved, matched by migration name. Without it, Jellyfin re-ran routines that expect `library.db` and startup failed with `no such table: TypedBaseItems` (#9).
- The provider pins `QuerySplittingBehavior` to `SingleQuery`, matching Jellyfin's SQLite provider, and stops flooding the log with `MultipleCollectionIncludeWarning`.

Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 or newer, and .NET 10.

## Español

### 3.0.3 — Integraciones privadas, mantenimiento y estabilidad

- Nuevo host seguro para esquemas privados de plugins: registro, migraciones aisladas y acceso sin exponer credenciales ni el esquema `public` de Jellyfin.
- Nueva pestaña **Integraciones** para revisar esquemas registrados, consultar una muestra limitada de datos, ver métricas por tabla y administrar `ANALYZE`, `VACUUM (ANALYZE)` y `REINDEX` por esquema.
- Las tareas programadas mantienen `public` y solo los esquemas privados autorizados por el administrador.
- Health incorpora métricas de presión de buffers, bloques leídos, uso temporal y WAL para diagnosticar consultas lentas.
- Estado actual detecta el motor activo sin esperar la validación SQLite; esta continúa en segundo plano y se vuelve a comprobar antes de revertir.
- Se refuerza el aislamiento de identificadores en operaciones de exploración y mantenimiento de esquemas privados.
- Documentación actualizada en español e inglés, incluida la integración para desarrolladores, exportación SQLite segura y orientación para Docker.

Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 o posterior y .NET 10.

---

## English

### 3.0.3 — Private integrations, maintenance, and stability

- New secure host for private plugin schemas: registration, isolated migrations, and storage without exposing credentials or Jellyfin's `public` schema.
- New **Integrations** tab to review registered schemas, inspect a bounded data sample, view per-table metrics, and manage `ANALYZE`, `VACUUM (ANALYZE)`, and `REINDEX` per schema.
- Scheduled tasks maintain `public` and only private schemas explicitly enabled by an administrator.
- Health adds buffer-pressure, blocks-read, temporary-I/O, and WAL metrics for slow-query diagnosis.
- Current status detects the active engine without waiting for SQLite validation; validation continues in the background and is checked again before rollback.
- Strengthens identifier isolation in private-schema exploration and maintenance operations.
- Updated Spanish and English documentation, including developer integration, safe SQLite export, and Docker guidance.

Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16 or newer, and .NET 10.

## Español

### 3.0.2 — Estabilidad, integridad y exportación segura

- Corrige la normalización de `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset` y arreglos antes de escribir en PostgreSQL, evitando errores de Npgsql por `Kind` incompatible.
- Las escrituras concurrentes de `UserData` y las actualizaciones completas de elementos usan upserts atómicos para reducir conflictos durante actualizaciones bajo demanda.
- La activación de PostgreSQL valida la conexión antes de modificar `database.xml`.
- Se elimina la restauración automática de backups y la restauración manual no reemplaza objetos existentes por defecto.
- Las consultas concurrentes idénticas de inicio se consolidan mientras se llena la caché.
- La exportación PostgreSQL → SQLite crea y valida un `library.db` SQLite real; evita el archivo inválido que impedía iniciar Jellyfin.
- La exportación ya no copia ni marca a ciegas el historial de migraciones.

Verificado con Build Release, pruebas unitarias e integración real contra PostgreSQL. Requiere Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16+ y .NET 10.

## English

### 3.0.2 — Stability, integrity and safe export

- Fixes normalization of `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, and arrays before PostgreSQL writes, avoiding Npgsql errors caused by incompatible `Kind` values.
- Concurrent `UserData` writes and full item updates use atomic upserts to reduce conflicts during on-demand updates.
- PostgreSQL activation validates the connection before changing `database.xml`.
- Automatic backup restore was removed, and manual restore no longer replaces existing objects by default.
- Identical concurrent home-screen queries are coalesced while the cache is populated.
- PostgreSQL → SQLite export creates and validates a real SQLite `library.db`, preventing the invalid file that stopped Jellyfin from starting.
- Export no longer blindly marks or copies migration history.

Verified with a Release build, unit tests, and real PostgreSQL integration tests. Requires Jellyfin 12.1.x, PostgreSQL 16+, and .NET 10.

versions.changelog:
feat: choose video and audio codec for transcoded downloads

- The quality sheet now offers a video and an audio codec picker, limited to
  what the server actually has enabled
- Downloads started from an episode list target the episode whose menu you
  opened, instead of the season or series the page is showing
- Failed or empty transcodes now report the real HTTP status instead of
  silently producing a broken file
fix: transcoding actually respects selected quality tier.
fix: i18n strings now load in the correct Jellyfin UI language (de, us, es, fr, nl, zh-cn)

Fix queue panel resetting progress bar when new items are added

Incremental DOM updates replace full re-renders so the active download's
progress bar is preserved when a second item joins the queue.

Add multi-download queue

Downloads now enqueue instead of starting immediately. Each queued item has its own cancel button; cancelling removes only that item and the next starts automatically. The bottom-right panel shows all queued items with live progress for the active one. Queue is in-memory only.
Update logo, rename console prefix to [TranscodeDownloader], fix README and manifest

Fix transcode quality tiers and stale item on first page load

- On first load, quality sheet now awaits metadata before building the
  tier list, so only valid bitrates (below source bitrate) are shown
- Quality sheet now re-derives the item ID from the URL at open time,
  preventing downloads targeting the previous movie when navigating
  between items before the hash-change event fires

Replace dropdown button with action sheet menu entry

- Remove injected select+button from the detail page
- Add 'Download (Transcode…)' entry to Jellyfin's native 'Mehr' menu
- Quality selection via a second overlay in Jellyfin's action sheet style
- Fixes reload-required bug; no longer disrupts the detail page layout

fix: show plugin logo in catalog and installed plugin detail page

- Add imageUrl to manifest.json so the catalog displays the logo
- Include logo.png in the release zip for the installed plugin detail page

rename: QuickDownload → Transcode Downloader + add logo and build CI

- Plugin display name is now "Transcode Downloader"
- All internals renamed to Jellyfin.Plugin.TranscodeDownloader
- Controller route changed to /TranscodeDownloader/ClientScript
- Added logo.png
- Added PR build workflow

Fix: force transcode to honour selected quality tier

Without allowVideoStreamCopy=false Jellyfin could direct-stream the
original file, ignoring MaxStreamingBitrate and MaxHeight entirely.
Downloads now correctly re-encode to the selected resolution and bitrate.

Fix: force transcode to honour selected quality tier

Without allowVideoStreamCopy=false Jellyfin could direct-stream the
original file, ignoring MaxStreamingBitrate and MaxHeight entirely.
Downloads now correctly re-encode to the selected resolution and bitrate.
fix: delay revokeObjectURL to prevent download failure after completion

fix: button appears on first load without page reload

Replace 20x250ms polling retry loop with a MutationObserver that fires
the moment Jellyfin's SPA renders the detail-view container. The old
loop could time out before the SPA finished hydrating, requiring a
manual page reload to see the download button.

fix: use ApiClient.getItem() for metadata fetch to avoid 401

Jellyfin 10.11 rejects api_key query-param auth on the Items endpoint,
causing the dropdown to stay empty. Switch to client.getItem() which
sends the correct Authorization header.

fix: populate dropdown after UI injection to eliminate race condition

The metadata fetch often completed before Jellyfin rendered the detail
container, so populateDropdown() exited early (select === null) without
ever setting currentItem. Clicking Download then silently did nothing.

- Move currentItem assignment before the early return in populateDropdown()
- Re-call populateDropdown() after injecting the UI if data already arrived
- Reset currentItem when navigating to a new item to avoid stale options

fix: strip Accept-Encoding/Content-Encoding to prevent compressed-body corruption

Jellyfin's static file middleware serves index.html pre-compressed when the
client advertises Accept-Encoding. The IStartupFilter middleware was buffering
those compressed bytes and writing them back with Content-Encoding: gzip still
set, causing browsers to report 'cannot decode raw data'.

Fix: remove Accept-Encoding from the request before intercepting so upstream
never activates compression; also strip Content-Encoding from the response.

fix: inject script tag via middleware — button now appears without companion plugins

The script tag is now injected by an ASP.NET Core IStartupFilter that
intercepts index.html responses in Jellyfin's HTTP pipeline. No File
Transformation plugin required, no disk writes, no timing sensitivity.

Also fixes plugin loading error in the admin UI (Plugin constructor now
calls SetAttributes).

fix: call SetAttributes in Plugin constructor so CanUninstall doesn't throw

BasePlugin (non-generic) never calls SetAttributes — only BasePlugin<T> does
in its own constructor. Without it, AssemblyFilePath stays null, and
CanUninstall throws NullReferenceException when GET /Plugins serializes the
plugin list, breaking the admin plugins page on every page load.

Fix: inject IApplicationPaths and call SetAttributes the same way BasePlugin<T>
does, giving Jellyfin a valid assembly path and data folder path.

Serve client script from controller and inject in-memory

- QuickDownloadController serves the embedded plugin.js at GET /QuickDownload/ClientScript (AllowAnonymous) so the web root never needs to be writable
- WebAssetInjector registers an in-memory File Transformation callback instead of patching index.html on disk; survives Jellyfin web updates and is auto-removed on plugin uninstall
- On-disk fallback retained for installs without File Transformation, with a loud actionable log recommending FT >= v2.2.1.0
- Base-path-aware script src for Jellyfin deployments behind a sub-path

- The in-browser slider is now labelled **All themes**, and carries a tooltip saying it applies
  to every title and to your account only. It always worked that way; appearing over a
  particular series just made it look like a per-series control.
- The per-user settings page says the same thing in the same words.
- The slider now stays up for as long as a theme is actually playing, instead of fading after a

  the file on disk. That was the one part of the plugin that did not work on a normal package
  install, where the web client is owned by root and Jellyfin runs as its own user - and it
  also means a Jellyfin upgrade can no longer undo it.
- The old on-disk patch is still selectable under **Web client -> How the script gets in**, and

- Replaced play-count rewatch boost with recency-driven Recent Watch Emphasis using decay-squared amplification (#20); the RewatchBoost setting becomes RecentWatchBoost (default 1.0)
- Config page numeric fields saved as 0 no longer revert to defaults (#22)
- REQUIRES Jellyfin 10.11.9 or newer

Migrate from .strm files to filesystem symlinks (#13)
- Fixes transcoded playback on Jellyfin 10.11.7+ (GHSA-j2hf-x4q5-47j3)
- Symlinks preserve source extensions; media pipeline treats them as regular files
- Artwork symlinked from source folder (propagates custom posters automatically)
- Trailer discovery delegated to Jellyfin's native scanner
- Removed ImageSyncService and EnableImageSync/SyncBackdrops settings
- WINDOWS: requires Administrator or Developer Mode enabled for symlink creation

Filter recommendations by user library access (#10)
- Items from libraries a user cannot access are excluded from recommendations
- Applies to both personalized and cold-start recommendation paths
- Respects per-user library permissions including disabled libraries

Fix playback freeze when playing from recommendation libraries (#8)
- Never remove virtual library items from event handlers (deferred to next refresh)
- Ignore PlaybackStart/PlaybackProgress events to prevent DB write storms during playback
- Only sync play status on meaningful events (PlaybackFinished, TogglePlayed, etc.)
- Known tradeoff: partially watched items may appear in Continue Watching twice until next refresh

Bug fixes for series recommendations and playback crashes
- Fixed: Partially watched series not included in watch history, causing all users to get identical cold-start recommendations (#7)
- Fixed: Playback from recommendation libraries crashing with database failures (#8)
- Series watch history now detected at episode level instead of requiring all episodes watched
- Virtual library items no longer removed during active playback

Image sync for custom posters and backdrops
- Custom poster images are now preserved in recommendation libraries
- Copies poster.jpg and backdrop.jpg from source items to virtual folders
- Configurable: Enable/disable image sync and backdrop copying
- Fixes issue where user customizations (e.g., French posters) were lost

Decade-based temporal similarity and bug fix
- Recommendations now consider content from similar time periods
- Decade grouping (1980s, 1990s, etc.) replaces continuous year normalization
- Improves temporal relevance alongside genre/actor/director similarity
- Tested with production data: ~12 decades extracted from 970 items
- Observable impact: 24% of movie recommendations changed, 8% of TV
- Fixed: In-progress TV series no longer appear in recommendations

Series filtering fix and play status sync
- Fixed fully watched series appearing in recommendations
- Play status sync from source library when virtual items are scanned
- Rating proximity scoring feature
- Removed NFO file generation (Jellyfin doesn't read NFO for .strm files)
- Reduced debug logging noise

Fix NFO metadata parsing
- Fixed XML encoding (UTF-16 to UTF-8) so Jellyfin reads runtime correctly
- Added cast, directors, and writers to NFO files
- Added fileinfo/streamdetails for video/audio/subtitle stream selectors

NFO metadata and trailer support
- NFO files with full metadata (runtime, ratings, genres, studios, tags)
- Local trailer support via -trailer.strm files
- Movie folder structure for better metadata handling
- Fixed copy buttons on setup page
- Improved documentation

Initial beta release
- Per-user personalized recommendations for movies and TV shows
- Content-based filtering using TF-IDF embeddings
- Virtual library integration for universal client compatibility
- Configurable weighting (favorites, rewatches, recency)
- Abandoned series exclusion
- Daily scheduled updates with manual refresh option
- Complete privacy - all processing local

description:

The result is plain CSS written to Branding > Custom CSS; optional script features (toolbar buttons, slideshow, card badges) through File Transformation.

Github: https://github.com/SpeeDFireCZE/jellycanvas
