versions.changelog:
**Drop-down menus in the theme's look, and a title over the poster that
makes way for the hover buttons.** Jellyfin's drop-down fields - the item
page's audio and subtitle menus, "Add to playlist", the settings - showed
the browser's own grey list; in Chrome and Edge they now take the Dialogs &
menus look and open downwards. With the title printed over the poster, the
watched / favorite / menu buttons were hidden under it and greyed by its
gradient; the title now fades (or slides) away while the pointer is on the
card. All of it is plain CSS, so "CSS only" has it too.

Updating is enough - the plugin brings the CSS in Branding up to date at
startup, and open pages pick it up on their own (a browser holding the old
page in its cache may need one Ctrl+F5).

Drop-down menus

- Dialogs & menus: Jellyfin's drop-down fields take the menus' look - style, color, opacity, blur, corners - with the chosen entry marked in the accent: the item page's version / video / audio / subtitle menus, "Add to playlist" (the one music users meet) and "Add to collection", the user settings for the home screen, playback and subtitles, the metadata editor. They are native selects, and on a computer or a phone the browser drew their list itself, in its own grey, out of any theme's reach. Chrome and Edge (135 and up) now draw it as part of the page (`appearance: base-select`); other browsers keep their own list, in the theme's colors. The TV opens Jellyfin's own menu, which was themed already. Plain CSS, so "CSS only" has it too.
- The lists open downwards. The browser picks the side with more room, so a field in the lower row of the item page opened upwards; below comes first now, a list that does not fit there gets shorter (it scrolls), and only a field at the very bottom of the window opens upwards.

Cards

- Cards: with the title over the image, the hover buttons (watched, favorite, menu) appeared under it - both sit in the bottom corner, and the title lay on top and took their clicks. The title now makes way while the pointer is on the card: it fades out (the default) or slides down as it fades, and comes back when the pointer leaves. The choice is under the title setting (*Cards → The title when the pointer is on the card*, shown for "Over the image" while the hover buttons are on); "Stays" keeps it as before. Only where the buttons appear - not on the TV or a phone, not on series, seasons and collections whose buttons are hidden, and not on the Seerr rows' cards (their button sits in the middle). Plain CSS, so it works with "CSS only" too.
- Fixed: with the title over the image the hover buttons and the bottom card badges were grey and dull - the dark gradient under the title was painted over them (the same layer, and last in the card). It lies under them now, and while the title makes way the gradient goes with it; Jellyfin's own veil over a hovered card stays.

**A theme applied shows at once, the music player follows the theme, and
"CSS only" is CSS only everywhere.** Jellyfin's client held the branding
CSS for a minute, so open pages kept the old theme after an Apply; the
client script now swaps in the fresh one - on the next navigation within a
second, on a page left open within ten. The music player takes the Player
section's look - until now its bar and sliders stayed in Jellyfin's grey
and blue whatever the theme said. Applied, "CSS only" takes the admin look
off the plugin page at once, the CSS it writes holds nothing for the admin
pages, and a theme exported in that mode is a CSS theme, so an import gives
the same look. Plus a fix for the Sidebar layout, which broke the admin
pages when they followed the defaults.

Updating is enough - the plugin brings the CSS in Branding up to date at
startup, and the client script's address carries the version, so a fresh
page load picks the new one up (a browser holding the old page in its cache
may need one Ctrl+F5).

A theme applied reaches open pages at once

- Fixed: a theme just applied took a minute or more to show on the user-facing pages - on the admin pages it was there at once. Jellyfin's client keeps the branding CSS it fetched for a minute before it asks again (and a tab left open did not ask until something nudged it). The theme block now carries a stamp, a new `/Jellycanvas/CssStamp` tells the current one in a few bytes, and the client script asks for it when a page loads, on every navigation, when the window or the tab comes back, and every ten seconds while the page is in view; it also watches the client's copy, which the client renders again after a navigation. An older copy is switched off and the fresh CSS goes in over it until the client catches up - a navigation shows the new theme within a second, a page just left open within ten. With "CSS only" there is no script, and Jellyfin's minute stays.
- The client script runs for an applied theme even without a feature of its own (that check is its job then).
- The startup refresh compares the stamp: the date line in the block made it rewrite Branding on every start, even with nothing changed.

The music player

- The music player follows the Player section: its bar along the bottom takes the control bar's style (solid, glass, gradient and the rest, its color, opacity, blur), floats and rounds like it, and its buttons take the buttons' size. The position and volume sliders - in the bar and on the queue page - take the progress slider's color and the position ones its height. Until now all of it stayed in Jellyfin's stock grey and hard-coded blue.
- Sliders anywhere else (a settings page, say) take the accent instead of Jellyfin blue.
- Fixed: with the Sidebar layout the music bar ran under the sidebar and covered its bottom (the user button among it); it starts where the content does now.
- Test server: `test\Make-Music.ps1` adds a music library - three made-up albums of generated tones, tagged and with covers - to check the music pages against a theme.

CSS only

- Fixed: after "CSS only" was applied, the plugin page itself - an admin page - kept the custom Dashboard look until it was reloaded. The client script running in it went on with what it had fetched when the page loaded. The designer now swaps it for what the server serves after every Apply and every Remove: nothing after CSS only (the admin pages turn stock at once), and the fresh admin look after an ordinary Apply, which until now also waited for a reload.
- CSS only: the theme no longer writes its rules for the admin pages - without the script they never reach them (Jellyfin renders Branding on the user-facing pages only), so they were dead weight.
- Share: a theme exported in "CSS only" mode carries the CSS look only. The script's features were hidden from its author, yet the export took whatever they still held (from before the switch, or from an import) - so an import brought a slideshow, badges or an admin look nobody had seen with that theme. The admin pages are left out now (their panel settings, "Theme the Dashboard" and the Dashboard tab's document), and of the script's features only their switches go along, turned off (the slideshow, the badges, the item page's banner, the info bar's close button) - an import gives the same CSS version, and the theme site no longer lists such a theme as needing File Transformation or styling the admin pages. The importer's own "CSS only" choice, buttons and Seerr stay theirs, as before. The Share section says so while CSS only is on.
- Designer: unticking "CSS only" brings the script features back into the preview straight away; until now they came back only with the next change to a script setting.

The admin pages

- Fixed: with the Sidebar layout and the theme on the Dashboard, the admin pages fell apart - their top bar was turned into the sidebar column and went off the screen, and the content slid under the admin menu. The admin pages have a menu of their own on the left, so the sidebar now stays on the user-facing pages and the admin bar docks next to the menu as before. The Dashboard tab no longer offers a layout either; it shows the bar's own settings.

The designer

- Designer: rows show where they do something - the "Play" label only while the other buttons have no labels (with labels on, Play has one anyway), the logo's height for the Jellyfin icon or a custom image and its width for a custom image only, and the info bar's settings only while the bar is on.

**The loading ring gets a look of its own, and a season's episodes get
their badges.** The ring Jellyfin shows while a stream starts can take one
of six styles, a color, size, speed, a glow and a disc behind it - and even
left alone it now follows the theme's accent instead of Jellyfin blue. The
episodes on a season's page carry the card badges, the home slideshow's
button picks its icon from a list, and the Dashboard's device cards lose
the dark boxes a lighter now-playing veil left behind their text.

Updating is enough - the plugin brings the CSS in Branding up to date at
startup, and the client script's address carries the version, so a fresh
page load picks the new one up (a browser holding the old page in its cache
may need one Ctrl+F5).

The player

- Player: the loading ring - the one Jellyfin shows while a stream starts (and, being the same element, while a page loads) - has settings of its own (Player -> Loading ring): Jellyfin's ring, a ring, a double ring, an orbiting dot, a pulse or three dots; its color (empty = the accent), size, line thickness and speed; a glow in its color; and a dark or frosted disc behind it. The player preview shows it in the middle, and Ctrl+click on it opens these settings. Jellyfin paints its ring blue by hard-coded value, so even untouched it now takes the theme's accent.

Home slideshow

- Home slideshow: the button's icon is picked from a list - info, play, play in a circle, a screen with play, arrows, open, eye, film strip, cinema, compass, star, heart, three dots, or none - with the chosen icon shown next to the label. "Another one" brings back the name field for any Material icon, and a theme with an icon outside the list opens with that field.
- Fixed: the home slideshow's button style did nothing in the designer's preview - the button kept the look it had when the slideshow first appeared. Security and speed

- Security: the random background picks only items every enabled account may see. Its address is anonymous (the login page uses it, and a CSS `url()` cannot carry a token), so it cannot tell who is looking - and until now it could put a backdrop from a library a child's account is kept out of, or one rated above that account's limit, on the login page or behind that child's home screen. Library access, the parental rating and blocked tags of every account are respected now.
- Security: text the theme writes into a CSS string (the `content:` of a label) loses every control character, not just line breaks - a form feed also ends a CSS string and would let the rest of the text be read as rules.
- Security: the settings baked into the client script escape `<`, `>`, `&` and `'` (before, only `</` was defused), so the script stays whole even when pasted inline into an HTML page by an injector plugin. Letters of every language stay readable.
- Faster: "Slow panning animation" moves the picture's layer instead of the picture inside it. It animated `background-position`, which makes the browser restyle and repaint a full-screen picture every frame; a `transform` runs on the compositor. A home page at rest with a panning random background went from about 120 ms of main-thread work per 8 seconds to 16 ms (Chrome, desktop) - on a weak TV it was most of what the page cost. It looks the same, portrait phones included.
- Seerr posters: the disk cache no longer grows for ever - posters nobody asked for in 30 days go (checked at most once a day). A poster is written aside and moved in whole, so two requests at once never read a half-written file; after a server restart a poster already on disk is served straight away instead of a 404 until Seerr has answered again; a download is capped at 4 MB.

  glowing or Jellyfin's own grow, without running into its neighbours;
  TV cards are rounded like the others.
- The designer: group headings and the open section stand out.
- Fixed: the split bar's surface ran across the whole library row; a
  panning backdrop was a band across the middle of a phone screen; the
  info bar's close button floated above a custom button's overlay; the
  theme's background (rotating backdrops) covered the video while it
  played; the player's progress slider now follows the accent color; the
  CSS no longer uses the `inset` shorthand (older TV browsers).
- README: screenshots from the demo.
- Release workflow: with a `RELEASE_TOKEN` secret the release and the
  manifest commit are made under its owner's account.

- Card badges: the Colorful style gives every value its own color (4K
  pink, 1080p blue, 720p green, SD grey; DV / HDR / HLG; HEVC, H264, AV1...;
  a color per sound family; a color per language) with a choice of range:
  vivid, cool, warm, pastel, neon. Badges in a corner that holds Jellyfin's
  own indicator (played tick, unplayed count, media source) start under it.
- Info bar: *Hide on TV*; the close button's memory is a choice - remember
  the close until the text changes (as before), or show the strip again
  on every page load.
- Fixed: two custom buttons on the same side of the bar kept swapping
  places on every sync and never received a click.
- Fixed: closing the info bar in the designer's preview hid it for the
  admin on the site as well (same browser storage); the preview now keeps
  its closes to itself and *Apply* clears a remembered close in the
  admin's browser.
- The theme import lives in *Share / import* only (it was also in the
  Extra CSS section for a while).

A bug-fix release, with the TV layout and theme sharing on top.

- TV layout: the preview really starts the client in its TV layout, and
  the bar settings reach the TV's own top bar (style, islands, floating,
  rounding, shadow, navigation pills / underline, hidden icons, logo);
  bar height and icon size under *TV*; the tabs stay inside the bar at
  any height; the info bar sits under the bar; custom toolbar buttons
  show on TV when allowed (icons before the search, links next to the
  logo) and their overlay opens below the bar.
- Mobile: the bar stays on one row (the user icon used to drop under an
  islands bar); a custom link in the slide-out menu opens again.
- Background: a random backdrop rotation cross-fades smoothly between
  images (script) instead of cutting.
- Info bar: long text wraps onto more lines, on phones too, and the page
  moves down for it.
- Share / import: a theme can be imported from a link (a raw GitHub
  file, for example) - also from the *Extra CSS, export & import*
  section. The export carries only the look: custom buttons and their
  addresses, the info bar text, the login title, the uploaded logo and
  image links on private addresses stay out of it.
- Fixed: the TV info bar overlapped the top bar; a rotation stopped while
  an image was loading threw an error.
- Old theme files: a server upgraded from 10.x can be left with the old
  `web/themes/*/theme.css`, which does not read the `--jf-*` variables -
  the palette and the card rounding were ignored there. The generated CSS
  now carries the theme stylesheet's variable rules itself (a no-op on a
  current install), the card rounding is also written straight onto the
  card elements, and *Misc → Theme files on the server* lists which files
  are old and can patch them (a copy is kept as `theme.css.jellycanvas-bak`).
- Fixed: with *Apply to dark themes only*, every rule starting with `html`
  (bar, cards, TV, mobile - a third of the theme) was generated as
  `html:not(...) html ...` and never applied.
- Fixed: the corner-badge played style sat inset from the corner on
  rounded cards; its icon and the unplayed count now keep clear of the
  rounded corner.
- Development: `test\Make-Media.ps1` regenerates the test clips with
  resolutions, HDR, audio languages and subtitles so the badges have
  something to show; the test scripts run on Jellyfin 12.1.

- Card badges: audio and subtitle languages each have their own style -
  audio as flags and subtitles as codes by default, so the flags are not
  repeated for the subtitles.

- Plugin logo, shown in the catalog and the plugin list.
- Card badges: video codec and sound (Dolby Digital+ 5.1, DTS-HD 7.1...)
  badges; badges of a corner stacked under each other; a color-per-kind
  style; languages as bare flags (each language its own flag), codes, or
  both.
- Item page: description & info blocks - every block (selectors,
  overview, genres, tags, external links) can sit on a background of its
  own with its own color; a chip color for the whole section.
- Fixed: a glow or neo-brutalist title ribbon made the title, year and
  rating vanish (the surface now sits on a layer behind the content);
  Jellyfin's played / count indicators and the badges keep clear of
  rounded card corners; the search link on library pages no longer moves
  custom toolbar buttons.
- Versions are three-part from now on (1.0.1).

First public release, for Jellyfin 12.0.

Designer

- Companion plugins panel at the top: which of File Transformation /
  JavaScript Injector is installed and what each unlocks; the sections
  that need one stay hidden without it.
- Settings page in the Dashboard with a live preview of the real web
  client for the web, TV and mobile layouts; the preview follows the
  setting being changed and can show the player's "Up next" and "Still
  watching?" prompts; Ctrl+click on anything in the preview jumps to its
  setting.
- Save draft (private) / Apply to server / Remove from server; the CSS
  goes to Branding → Custom CSS between marker comments and never touches
  CSS you wrote yourself.
- Presets, Share / import of themes as JSON, editable numbers next to
  every slider, English UI with a Czech translation.

Theme

- Colors, typography (bundled, system or any Google Fonts family).
- Bar: full-width top bar, top bar split into islands, or a vertical
  sidebar (optionally collapsible); solid / glass / gradient / transparent
  / neo-brutalism / glowmorphism / claymorphism / neumorphism; rounding,
  floating, shadow, height; draggable arrangement of the logo + links,
  icons and user groups; navigation link styles; hide icons; library row
  look next to a sidebar; logo by URL or upload.
- Info bar (announcement strip) at the top or bottom.
- Cards: rounding, hover effects, shadow, border, text placement,
  spacing, watched-item and progress styles (incl. a translucent fill),
  hover buttons off everywhere or only on series / seasons / collections.
- Buttons & inputs, Play button, dialogs & menus (and the player's "Up
  next" prompt).
- Item detail page: title ribbon style, poster, cast & crew as circles /
  squares, selectors / genres / tags / links as chips, overview size,
  section titles, hide sections.
- Background image: random library backdrop rotating every N seconds,
  custom URL, blur, dim, panning.
- Login page: background image or gradient over the whole page (no bar,
  just the logo), form as card / glass, field and button styles, custom
  heading, hide Quick Connect / Forgot password.
- Side menu (mobile drawer), TV focus, mobile tweaks, hide scrollbars,
  free-form extra CSS.

Script features (with File Transformation or a JS injector)

- Custom toolbar buttons (overlay, new tab or navigate) with a Material
  icon picker; on phones they go into the slide-out menu.
- Home slideshow (hero carousel from a query).
- Card badges: resolution, HDR, audio and subtitle languages in chosen
  corners of movie and episode cards.
- Close button on the info bar.

versions.changelog: v0.9.0 - Grande passe de durcissement issue d'un 3e audit ultra-complet (10 dimensions, revue adversariale multi-agents) : 6 corrections MEDIUM + ~29 durcissements LOW, 0 critique/eleve restant. Recommandee. PAS DE MIGRATION. Compatible Jellyfin 10.11.10 et 10.11.11. MEDIUM : (1) coller un emoji au ras d'une limite de longueur pouvait faire echouer la sauvegarde de config (500 ; troncature UTF-16 rune-safe) ; (2) annuler l'avertissement 'utilisateurs en streaming' n'efface plus silencieusement les modifs de l'onglet Maintenance et n'affiche plus un faux succes ; (3) modales Uptime Kuma / Import accessibles (role=dialog, focus piege, Echap, focus restitue) ; (4) reordonnancement des lignes au clavier (fleches haut/bas) ; (5) la couche d'enforcement anti-SSRF des webhooks est desormais couverte par des tests ; (6) le pipeline de release verifie que l'URL d'asset du manifest correspond (anti-typo de casse type v0.6.0). LOW notables : anti lost-update entre onglets, purge des utilisateurs supprimes du suivi 'vu', tailles de boutons bornees, coherence de planning fixe C#/JS, ARIA onglets + navigation fleches, contrastes et cibles tactiles WCAG, garde double-execution du script injecte, un seul fetch /maintenance par navigation, test de reflexion des tiers d'autorisation, coherence de version sur 4 sources. + 2 liens de documentation corriges. 391 tests verts, build 0 warning.

v0.8.5 - Corrections UX/a11y/fonctionnel issues d'un 2e audit ultra-complet (toutes couches : UX, design, perf, code, a11y, docs ; 0 critique restant, 6 high corriges ici). Recommande. HIGH : (1) les modeles rapides d'annonce (ex : Halloween/Noel 'annuel') perdaient silencieusement leur planning / auto-expiration / theme / image -> l'annonce s'affichait toute l'annee au lieu de sa fenetre ; desormais tous les champs sont copies. (2) L'overlay de maintenance plein ecran a enfin la meme accessibilite que les modales d'annonce : role=dialog + aria-modal, focus piege a l'interieur, scroll de la page verrouille, focus restitue a la fermeture (avant : un utilisateur clavier/lecteur d'ecran pouvait tabuler derriere l'overlay). (3) En mode carousel, les cartes non visitees n'etaient jamais marquees 'vues' -> le carousel reapparaissait a chaque connexion ; maintenant toutes les cartes sont marquees a la fermeture. (4) Un redemarrage programme a la fin de la fenetre de maintenance etait annule silencieusement par la desactivation auto du meme tick -> il se declenche desormais correctement. (5) `make bump` (outil de dev) etait casse sur GNU sed (Git Bash / CI Linux). (6) README : exigence Jellyfin corrigee 10.11.6 -> 10.11.10. MEDIUM : cap sur le NOMBRE d'elements des collections (annonces 200 / messages 100 / etc.) anti-bloat config.xml ; image hero d'annonce masquee si l'URL est morte (plus d'icone cassee) ; pluralisation '1 annonce'. TESTS : 366/366 verts (+3 caps), build 0 warning, revue adversariale multi-agents (aucune regression critique/elevee). Compatible Jellyfin 10.11.10 et 10.11.11. PAS DE MIGRATION.

v0.8.4 - Release de SECURITE + corrections (suite a un audit adverse multi-agents). Recommande pour tous. SECURITE (webhook SSRF, durci sur 3 couches) : la defense SSRF de v0.7.0 etait contournable. Corrige : (1) le HttpClient webhook suivait les redirections HTTP -> un hote public autorise pouvait renvoyer un 302 vers 169.254.169.254 (metadata cloud) / loopback / LAN ; desormais AllowAutoRedirect=false + un ConnectCallback qui re-valide l'IP REELLE de chaque connexion (bat aussi le DNS rebinding). (2) les litteraux IPv6-mappes (::ffff:169.254.169.254) et les hotes a point final (127.0.0.1.) contournaient la blocklist -> normalisation MapToIPv4 + trailing-dot. (3) ajout des plages ::, CGNAT 100.64/10, fec0::/10, broadcast. NB : configurer un webhook reste admin-only (RequiresElevation), donc l'attaque exige un admin malveillant ou piege. CORRECTIONS (audit) : (a) la desactivation manuelle de la maintenance n'est plus annulee par le planificateur (consommation du ScheduledStart passe + garde ScheduledEnd) ; (b) ajouter un user a la whitelist PENDANT la maintenance le reactive immediatement, le drift-check respecte la whitelist live ; (c) modele de concurrence APPLIQUE : tous les writers de config (SaveConfig/SaveMaintenance/SaveAdminAnnouncements/MarkSeen/ResetSeen + tache planifiee) passent par un verrou unique -> fin des pertes d'ecriture et du config.xml corrompu ; (d) les annonces recurrentes (daily/weekly/annual) sont evaluees en heure LOCALE serveur (etait UTC) -> elles s'affichent aux bonnes heures, alignees sur les bannieres (positionne le TZ du conteneur) ; (e) cap sur la taille de reponse webhook (anti-OOM) + try/catch global sur la tache planifiee ; (f) admin.js : fix d'une fuite de listeners (double-binding a chaque pageshow). CI : la garde ASCII attrape desormais U+2028/2029/0085 ; release.yml lance dotnet test avant de publier ; creation de release idempotente. TESTS : 363/363 verts (etait 316), correctifs SSRF mutation-verifies, revue adversariale multi-agents (aucune regression critique/elevee). PAS DE MIGRATION.

v0.8.3 - Release de durcissement qualite (reponse a un audit adverse). AUCUN changement de feature, AUCUN changement de comportement du plugin shippe : le DLL est fonctionnellement identique a v0.8.2. La seule modif du code shippe est un refactor interne behavior-preserving (extraction de MaintenanceHelper.SetUserDisabledAsync, la glue IUserManager.GetUserDto+UpdatePolicyAsync, factorisee depuis les 3 boucles activate/deactivate/drift-check) verifie equivalent par mutation testing. Tout le reste est de l'infra de test/CI qui ne part PAS dans le zip : (1) Garde anti-tests-vacuous via Stryker.NET (mutation testing) sur les helpers de logique pure (AnnouncementHelper + MaintenanceHelper), workflow dedie manuel+hebdo, seuil de non-regression. (2) +21 tests xUnit (295 -> 316) : durcissement HasUserSeen/MarkSeen, round-trip XML de PluginConfiguration (compat legacy + champs non-null), builders de payload webhook Discord/Slack/Generic, vecteurs XSS sur SAFE_URL_RE, et surtout 15 tests d'integration HTTP qui pilotent SaveConfig/SaveMaintenance/SaveAdminAnnouncements a travers un VRAI Plugin (BasePlugin sur dossier temp + XmlSerializer reel) avec preuve de persistance disque. (3) Smoke test de deploiement reel qui gate les releases : boot d'un vrai serveur Jellyfin (matrix 10.11.6 plancher targetAbi + 10.11.10 prod) avec le DLL monte, completion du wizard, auth admin, puis appel de /users-summary et /announcements/admin (les endpoints qui appellent IUserManager.GetUsers() - EXACTEMENT la methode qui crashait en MissingMethodException sur 10.11.9) + scan des logs serveur. Ce gate aurait attrape le bug v0.8.0 avant publication. TESTS : 316/316 verts sur SDK 10.11.10, refactor mutation-verifie (24/24 + nouveaux KILLED). PAS DE MIGRATION. Recommande pour 10.11.10+ ; equivalent fonctionnel a v0.8.2.

v0.8.2 - Compat refresh Jellyfin 10.11.10. Aucun changement de code, aucun changement de feature : juste un rebuild contre le SDK Jellyfin 10.11.10 (release patch sortie cote serveur) + bump targetAbi de 10.11.9.0 a 10.11.10.0 pour que Jellyfin 10.11.10+ accepte l'install sans warning. AUDIT API : diff complet de IUserManager + ISessionManager entre 10.11.9 et 10.11.10 = 0 difference, toutes les methodes utilisees (GetUsers, GetUserById, GetUserByName, GetUserDto, UpdatePolicyAsync, Sessions) ont signature identique. v0.8.1 (build 10.11.9) marche aussi sur 10.11.10 grace a la forward-compat Jellyfin meme-minor, mais ce binaire v0.8.2 est strictement aligne sur la derniere API. TESTS : 279/279 verts sur SDK 10.11.10. PAS DE MIGRATION. Si tu es sur Jellyfin <= 10.11.8, reste sur v0.8.0. Si tu es sur 10.11.9, v0.8.1 ou v0.8.2 marchent les deux. Si tu es sur 10.11.10+, v0.8.2 recommande.

v0.8.1 - HOTFIX CRITIQUE Jellyfin 10.11.9 : la propriete IUserManager.Users a ete supprimee dans Jellyfin 10.11.x (breaking change patch) au profit de la methode GetUsers(). Le plugin v0.8.0 (build contre SDK 10.11.6) crashait avec MissingMethodException 'Method not found: ... IUserManager.get_Users()' sur les routes /MaintenanceDeluxe/users-summary, /MaintenanceDeluxe/announcements/admin, et lors de l'activation maintenance (MaintenanceHelper.ActivateAsync). Pire : les exceptions remontaient dans les handlers ItemAdded/Updated/Removed de Jellyfin (via la stack DI partagee), cassant des fonctionnalites core du serveur. Fix : (1) bump Jellyfin.Controller + Jellyfin.Model de 10.11.6 -> 10.11.9 (csproj plugin ET csproj tests). (2) Remplacement de _userManager.Users par _userManager.GetUsers() sur 3 call sites : BannerController.GetUsersSummary (ligne 549), BannerController.GetAdminAnnouncements (ligne 704), MaintenanceHelper.ActivateAsync (ligne 138). (3) targetAbi du manifest passe de 10.11.6.0 a 10.11.9.0 - les serveurs Jellyfin sur 10.11.6/7/8 ne pourront plus installer v0.8.1+ via le manifest (downgrade SDK pas backward-compatible). Si tu es sur 10.11.6-8, reste sur v0.8.0 ou upgrade Jellyfin. TESTS : 279/279 verts sur le nouveau SDK 10.11.9 (aucune logique modifiee, juste l'API de IUserManager). PAS D'AUTRE CHANGEMENT cote feature - c'est strictement un hotfix de compat ABI.

v0.8.0 - Tour de fixes a11y + UX + CI robustesse (4 agents en parallele, +13 tests = 279 verts). A11Y: (1) Focus trap dans toutes les modales (dangerConfirm admin + showAnnouncementModal + Carousel + Stack banner.js) - Tab/Shift+Tab cycle dans la modale, capture/restore du document.activeElement. (2) Scroll lock body lors d'affichage modale annonce (overflow:hidden sur documentElement+body, restore au close). (3) Compteur carousel SR-friendly - counterEl cree une fois hors render() avec aria-atomic=true, mutation via textContent au lieu d'innerHTML wipe. (4) prefers-reduced-motion respecte (theme neon pulse, badge dirty pulse, jfDconfFade overlay animation, preview neon glow). (5) Contraste WCAG AA sur badges - draft #E8A33D->#FFD27A + opacity 0.18->0.28, expired #D9534F->#FF8A87 + opacity 0.15->0.30, expiring + schedule-incomplete aussi rehausses. (6) Touch targets 44x44 minimum sur .jf-dconf-btn (padding 8->12) et .jf-url-btn (padding 7->12 + min-height 44 + inline-flex). (7) Focus visible outline doree sur les inputs .jf-ann-field. (8) backdrop-filter fallback solide via @supports not (backdrop-filter) - fallback opaque pour vieux Chromium TV. UX: (9) Webhook test button desactive pendant la requete avec texte 'Test en cours...', reenable() partage entre then/catch. (10) Import config: _pendingImport=null sur Cancel/ESC/backdrop, garde Apply qui affiche feedback si pas de fichier selectionne, closeImportModal() centralise. (11) Release notes delete confirmation via dangerConfirm si la section a du contenu (titre/body/icon non vides), delete direct sinon. (12) Draft autosave: console.warn one-shot via _draftSaveFailed flag si quota localStorage depasse. (13) configPage.html: datetime-local placeholder='YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM' + pattern regex pour vieux Safari mobile sans support natif. INFRA: (14) escape_non_ascii.py utilise encoding='utf-8-sig' (strippe BOM auto). (15) check_version_coherence.py try/except sur parsing JSON/XML malformes -> exit 2 avec message clair. (16) WebhookNotifier SanitiseExceptionMessage + TryGetRetryAfterSeconds passees private->internal pour tests directs. TESTS: 13 nouveaux cas xUnit (SanitiseExceptionMessage 7 cas redaction URL+host, TryGetRetryAfterSeconds 4 cas null/cap60s/delta/pastdate, IsTargetedAtUser_DraftWithRoleAndUuidFilters regression guard, IsScheduleActive_Daily_MidnightWrap_ExactBoundaries). 266 v0.7.0 -> 279 v0.8.0. PAS DE MIGRATION : aucun nouveau champ, fixes defensifs uniquement.

v0.7.0 - Audit secondaire : 11 fixes (3 securite + 4 robustesse + 4 polish), 32 nouveaux tests xUnit (234 -> 266). (1) CRITIQUE banner.js checkTimeWindow overnight wrap : les banniers/annonces avec fenetre daily 22:00-06:00 retournaient toujours false, donc invisibles la nuit alors que le C# MatchesTimeWindow gerait correctement le wrap. Divergence client/serveur corrigee. (2) SSRF defense webhook URL : nouvelle helper IsWebhookHostSafe qui rejette loopback IPv4/IPv6 (127.0.0.0/8, ::1), link-local 169.254.0.0/16 (incl. AWS/Azure/GCP metadata endpoints), RFC1918 prive (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), IPv6 ULA fc00::/7, hostnames .localhost/.internal/.local, et localhost literal. Appliquee sur SaveMaintenance webhook URL ET TestWebhook endpoint. (3) WebhookNotifier log sanitization : SanitiseExceptionMessage strippe les URLs+tokens du message exception avant logging (LogWarning ne contient plus la URL discord avec son token). TestAsync retourne message generique a l'admin UI au lieu de ex.Message qui pouvait leak hostnames internes via SSL cert errors. (4) Init defensif Announcements + AnnouncementsSeen avec = new() property-level (en plus du constructeur) : XmlSerializer peut bypasser le constructeur sur XML legacy nil tags, laissant ces props null et causant NRE. (5) ValidateSchedules WeekDays empty/null : au lieu de rejeter (regression v0.6.1), auto-normaliser type='always'. Preserve la compat avec configs legacy qui avaient ce cas comme 'never-active' silencieux. (6) DetectFormat URL host parsing au lieu de substring match : avant, 'https://relay.com/discord-bot/api/webhooks/proxy' etait classifie Discord (faux positif). Maintenant utilise Uri.Host exact match (incl. canary.discord.com, ptb.discord.com). (7) GetActiveSessions snapshot ToList avant LINQ : evite race condition sur _sessionManager.Sessions collection mutable. (8) ClonePublicFields rendu internal + reutilise par MaintenanceScheduleTask au lieu de son snapshot field-by-field qui manquait ScheduledStart/End/ActivatedAt. (9) WebhookNotifier 429 Retry-After : respecte le header (en seconds ou HTTP-date), retry si <= 4s d'attente. (10) Webhook payload size cap 32KB : evite Discord/Slack/proxy 400 sur payloads trop gros (admin avec customTitle+customSubtitle+message tres longs). (11) banner.js tick() defensive null check sur CONFIG : si fetch /config fail (plugin disabled mid-session, network blip), CONFIG reste null et chaque CONFIG.* etait NRE. (12) LastModified monotone : Math.Max(old, now) protege contre les horloges qui reculent (NTP correction). TESTS : 32 nouveaux (15 cas checkTimeWindow overnight JS, 7 SSRF blocklist hosts, 6 boundary public ranges, 5 DetectFormat regression guards substring-match, ValidateSchedules WeekDays auto-correct 2 cas, NormaliseCssColor bounds revisited). 234 -> 266 verts.

v0.6.1 - Hotfix install + audit logique. (1) CRITIQUE: fix sourceUrl lowercase typo qui cassait l'installation Jellyfin de v0.6.0 (GitHub URLs case-sensitive, 'maintenance-deluxe' lowercase -> 404). (2) AUDIT FIXES: 7 trous logiques cibles par l'audit pre-v0.6.1. (a) CSS .theme-custom ajoutee a admin.css avec vars CSS dynamiques pour preview admin du theme personnalise (avant : preview affichait velours par defaut, le theme custom n'etait visible que sur le client final). (b) ValidateSchedules etendu : valide les bornes coherence interne sur les 3 types : 'fixed' rejette FixedStart >= FixedEnd, 'annual' rejette mois hors [1,12] ou jour hors [1,31], 'weekly' rejette weekDays empty ou jours hors [0,6]. Avant : admin pouvait save des schedules muets qui ne matchaient jamais. (c) PLUGIN_VERSION constante au top d'admin.js (etait hardcodee '0.3.2.0' depuis 7 versions). (d) Sélecteur 'Personnalisé' disable + opacity 0.4 + tooltip explicatif tant que customTheme=null, avec auto-fallback velours si l'admin avait setce le theme custom puis supprime sa config. (e) Badge schedule incomplet en rouge dashed ('Fenetre fixe non configuree', 'Annuel non configure', 'Hebdo (aucun jour)') au lieu du badge bleu trompeur. (f) expireAfterDays clamp client-side 1-365 avec mise a jour de l'input (plus de surprise quand le serveur reduit a 365). (g) NormaliseCssColor : case-insensitive sur rgba (RGBA(...) accepte) + validation bounds R/G/B in [0,255] (avant : rgb(256,0,0) accepte produisait du CSS invalide silencieux). (3) REFACTOR: SAFE_URL_RE constante module-level dans banner.js, remplace 4 regex dupliques identiques (XSS protocol-relative defense). (4) UX: 2 nouveaux ANN_TEMPLATES quick-add 'Soiree Halloween' (schedule annual Oct 25-Nov 1) et 'Fin d'annee' (schedule annual Dec 20-Jan 5 wrap), template 'Nouveaux films' expireAfterDays=14 prefilled. (5) DOCS: docs/announcements.md mis a jour avec tableau Phase 2 features (carousel/stack/draft/expire/schedule/image/viewport/custom theme), tableau complet des 19 champs Announcement avec types et defaults, 'truth matrix' AND-combined des filtres de livraison, projection serveur de /announcements/active expliquee. (6) TESTS xUnit : 21 nouveaux cas. ValidateSchedules Theory (fixed inverted, fixed open-ended, annual out-of-range 6 cas, annual wrap valide, weekly empty, weekly null, weekly out-of-range 3 cas, daily no-constraint), NormaliseCssColor Theory (RGBA case-insensitive 2, rgb out-of-range 3, boundary 1). 213 tests v0.6.0 -> 234 tests v0.6.1. PAS DE MIGRATION : aucun champ ajoute, fixes defensifs uniquement.

v0.6.0 - Phase 2 annonces complete : editeur de theme custom. Tu peux maintenant creer ton propre theme d'annonce avec ta palette / police / bordure preferes, sans toucher au code. Nouvelle classe CustomAnnouncementTheme persistee dans PluginConfiguration.CustomAnnouncementTheme avec 7 champs nullable : label, accentColor (hex), backdropColor (hex ou rgba), cardBackground (hex ou rgba), textColor (hex), fontFamily (whitelist : system|inter|jetbrains-mono|space-grotesk|manrope), borderStyle (whitelist : solid|glow|dashed|none). Champs vides = defaut Velours pour ce champ, donc partial customisation OK. 'custom' devient le 5eme thème dans la whitelist (selecteur global + override par annonce). Cote serveur : nouvelle helper NormaliseCustomAnnouncementTheme qui valide tous les champs et retourne null si tout est vide (drop automatique). Nouvelle helper NormaliseCssColor qui accepte hex + rgba() (necessaire pour les backdrops semi-transparents) avec regex strict anti-CSS-injection. Le client recoit le customTheme via /announcements/active, attache uniquement aux items qui ont theme='custom' (200 bytes economises par item sinon). Cote client banner.js : nouvelle fonction buildCustomThemeCss(t) qui genere les regles CSS dynamiquement, injectAnnTheme accepte un parametre customTheme avec re-injection auto quand le block change (admin tweak hot-reload via JSON signature). resolveAnnTheme retourne 'custom' tel quel (pas de fallback velours pour les annonces customisees). Le custom theme fonctionne dans les 3 modes (one-at-a-time, carousel, stack). Cote admin : nouveau bloc <details> repliable 'Editeur de theme personnalise' dans l'onglet Annonces avec 7 inputs grilles. v0.5.4 - Phase 2 annonces : viewport simulator admin. Au clic, l'iframe redimensionne en taille fixe et l'info dimensions s'affiche en bas de la toolbar. La selection persiste en localStorage (jf-md-vp-preset) donc l'admin garde son choix entre refresh. JS initViewportSimulator() ajoute au boot, wire les boutons de la toolbar, applique la classe + update les indicateurs (active + dimensions). v0.5.3 - Phase 2 annonces : image hero. Nouveau champ optionnel ImageUrl + ImageAlt sur Announcement, rendu sous forme d' entre le meta header et le body de la modale annonce. Memes regles d'URL safe que ctaUrl (http/https/relatif, pas de //host). Cap 2000 chars pour l'URL, 200 pour l'alt text. Si vide, aucune image rendue (comportement identique a v0.5.2). Cote client : tag avec loading='lazy', alt={imageAlt ou title de fallback}, border-radius:8px et bordure subtile coherente avec le card. CSS scope dans injectAnnouncementStyles. Cote admin : nouvelle fieldset 'Image (optionnelle)' avec deux inputs (URL + alt text). Live preview admin rend l'image en temps reel pour valider l'apparence avant publication. Validation server-side dans SaveAdminAnnouncements rejette les schemes non-safe avec un 400. Mode carousel : chaque slide affiche sa propre image. Mode stack : chaque carte empilee affiche sa propre image, scroll continue donc pas de souci de hauteur. 2 nouveaux tests xUnit (defaults + round-trip preservation a travers SelectDeliverableForUser). 183 tests v0.5.2 -> 185 tests v0.5.3 (+2).

v0.5.2 - Phase 2 annonces : Schedule fixed/annual/weekly/daily. Les annonces beneficient maintenant du meme systeme de planning que les rotation messages des bannieres. Cinq types : always (par defaut, pas de filtre), fixed (fenetre de date precise YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM start/end), annual (recurrent par mois/jour avec optional time window, gere le wrap d'annee comme Christmas Dec 20 -> Jan 5), weekly (jours de la semaine au choix + fenetre horaire), daily (juste une fenetre horaire quotidienne, gere les fenetres overnight 22:00->06:00). Implementation : nouvelle helper C# AnnouncementHelper.IsScheduleActive(schedule, now) qui mirror exactement le JS isInSchedule existant des banner messages. Filtre ajoute dans IsTargetedAtUser. Validation SaveAdminAnnouncements reutilise ValidateSchedules existant. UI : fieldset 'Planning' ajoutee dans l'editeur d'annonce, reutilise les helpers getScheduleDetailHtml + wireScheduleEditor + populateSchedule + collectSchedule existants des rotation messages (composant identique, juste rendu dans un contexte different). Badge summary 'Planning' bleu affiche en plus du badge etat quand schedule != always : 'Fenetre fixe' / 'Annuel' / 'Hebdo: Lu Ma Me' / 'Quotidien 09:00-17:00'. Le client recoit la liste deja filtree, aucune logique client modifiee. 14 nouveaux tests xUnit couvrent IsScheduleActive : null/always (3 cas), fixed avec bornes ouvertes/fermees (4 cas), annual avec year-wrap Christmas (3 cas), weekly day-of-week + empty list (3 cas), daily avec overnight window Theory (8 cas), unknown type fallback, integration IsTargetedAtUser_RespectsSchedule. 169 tests v0.5.1 -> 183 tests v0.5.2 (+14).

v0.5.1 - Phase 2 annonces : brouillon + auto-expire. Deux nouveaux champs admin pour reduire la friction sur les annonces (preparation a l'avance + nettoyage automatique). (1) BROUILLON : nouveau toggle 'Brouillon' dans l'editeur, separe de Active. Une annonce en brouillon reste visible dans la liste admin avec un badge orange dashed, mais le serveur ne la sert jamais aux users finaux meme si Active est coche. Permet de preparer le contenu d'une annonce a l'avance puis de la publier en un clic en decochant Brouillon. Filtre serveur ferme dans AnnouncementHelper.IsTargetedAtUser : draft -> not delivered. (2) AUTO-EXPIRE : nouveau champ 'Expire apres (jours)' (1-365, vide = jamais). Quand renseigne, le serveur filtre automatiquement les annonces dont PublishedAt + ExpireAfterDays est passe. Filtrage stateless dans AnnouncementHelper.IsExpired : pas de mutation, pas d'auto-archive (l'annonce reste visible en admin avec un badge rouge barre 'Expiree' pour que l'admin sache pourquoi elle n'est plus servie). Cas limites : 0 ou negatif = traite comme 'no expiration' (drop a la sauvegarde par le clamp serveur). PublishedAt null = jamais expire (safe default). (3) BADGES SUMMARY : la pilule a droite de chaque ligne annonce affiche maintenant 5 etats possibles : Active (vert), Inactive (gris), Brouillon (orange dashed), Expiree (rouge barre), Active (Xj) (orange si <=7 jours avant expiration). Priorite : draft > expired > inactive > active. (4) VALIDATION SERVEUR : POST /announcements/admin clamp ExpireAfterDays a 1-365 (>365 -> 365, <=0 -> null) pour eviter typos 365000 ou negatif qui creerait une annonce permanenly-expired. IsDraft est un bool simple. (5) TESTS : 13 nouveaux cas xUnit couvrant draft never-delivered, expired filtre, IsExpired boundaries (-10j, -7j exact, -3j, 0j, days=0, days=-5), null PublishedAt safe default, integration SelectDeliverableForUser. 156 tests v0.5.0 -> 169 tests v0.5.1 (+13).

v0.5.0 - Phase 2 annonces partielle : modes carousel et stack enfin actifs cote client. Depuis v0.3.9 (Phase 1), le selecteur 'Mode d'affichage' de l'admin offrait 3 choix (one-at-a-time / carousel / stack) mais le client retombait toujours sur one-at-a-time quel que soit le reglage. v0.5.0 ferme la promesse : (1) CAROUSEL : si plusieurs annonces non vues a delivrer, le client affiche UNE modale avec deux chevrons gauche/droite et un compteur '1 / N' en bas. Chaque slide a son propre theme et accent applique a l'overlay (palette + police + animation), le marquage 'vu' fire-and-forget se fait quand on quitte la slide via fleches OU au close final. Navigation clavier : fleche gauche/droite, ESC pour fermer. Sur mobile (<=700px), les chevrons collapsent en bas de l'ecran. (2) STACK : toutes les annonces empilees verticalement dans une seule modale scrollable, avec header 'N annonces' et un seul bouton sticky 'Tout marquer comme vu' en bas. Pas de bouton 'Compris' par carte, c'est le bouton global qui POST /seen sur les N IDs en parallele. Mode utile quand l'admin a beaucoup d'annonces non-critiques regroupees. (3) Edge case respecte : si une seule annonce non-vue est disponible, le mode est ignore et on retombe sur la modale classique (pas de carousel-a-1-slide ridicule ni de stack-a-1-carte vide). REFACTOR : extraction de buildAnnouncementCardHtml(a, withOk) (fonction pure, retourne le HTML de la carte) et createAnnouncementOverlay(themeKey, accent) (cree l'overlay vide). Reutilises par les 3 modes (one-at-a-time + carousel + stack). buildAnnouncementModal devient un wrapper de 5 lignes. CSS : 26 nouvelles regles scopees via #jf-ann-overlay.jf-ann-carousel et #jf-ann-overlay.jf-ann-stack, zero impact sur le mode one-at-a-time existant (aucune regression sur v0.4.1). TESTS : aucun changement cote backend C# (la logique de selection annonce/mode est deja faite cote serveur). 156 tests xUnit toujours verts. Les pieges (banner.js ASCII-safe, escape \u2039 \u203a pour les chevrons) appliques.

v0.4.1 - Audit complet de revue de code apres v0.4.0 : 14 fixes appliques (1 securite + 13 qualite/perf/UX), 0 changement de comportement attendu pour les configs valides. SECURITE : (1) Faille XSS via URL protocol-relative dans les liens Markdown des annonces et des bannieres : `[click](//evil.com)` etait accepte par le regex `^(https?:\/\/|\/)` et generait `<a href="//evil.com">` qui navigue vers l'host attaquant. Fix client (banner.js linkSafeUrl + safeUrl ligne 510 + ctaUrl ligne 1848 + annMdRender admin.js ligne 3196) et serveur (IsUrlSafe BannerController.cs) avec lookahead `\/(?!\/)` qui rejette explicitement `//host`. Nouveaux tests xUnit pour `//evil.com`, `//evil.com/path`, `///triple-slash`. QUALITE : (2) Validation manquante des couleurs CSS sur ColorPresets / BannerMessage.Bg|Color / PermanentEntry.Bg|Color dans SaveConfig - un admin pouvait persister `red;position:fixed;top:0` (XSS CSS via inline-style). Nouvelle helper NormaliseHexColorOrDefault avec fallback typiquement-defaut. 7 tests. (3) ValidateRoutes rejette desormais les sequences `..` et `//` consecutives (defence en profondeur, route patterns Jellyfin n'en contiennent jamais). 8 nouveaux tests. UX : (4) Nouvelle modale `dangerConfirm` pour les actions destructives (suppression annonce, reset seen, activation maintenance avec sessions actives en cours) : remplace `window.confirm` par une vraie modale avec liste des elements affectes, conseil contextuel, et delai 2-3s sur le bouton danger pour empecher les clics accidentels. Style CSS dedie (.jf-dconf-*) avec animation, ESC pour annuler. PERF : (5) Refactor SelectDeliverableForUser de O(announcements x seenEntries x usersPerEntry) a O(announcements + seenEntries) via HashSet lookup (50k comparaisons sur 1000 users x 50 annonces -> ~1k). Test stress sur 100 annonces / 50 entries seen. ROBUSTESSE : (6) maybeShowAnnouncements capture le token dans une closure et revalide via getToken() apres le delai 800ms : si l'user logout pendant ce delai, le fetch programme est abandonne au lieu de tirer avec l'ancien token. (7) banner.js efface l'overlay annonce existant avant d'en construire un nouveau (race rafetch rapide). (8) postMessage live-preview (admin->banner.js) cible window.location.origin au lieu de '*'. (9) banner.js coalesce les bursts de md-preview-update via setTimeout 33ms (~30fps) : un parent malveillant ou un auto-save buggy ne peut plus pegger le CPU. (10) updatePreview admin debounced 120ms par keystroke au lieu de re-parser le markdown a chaque touche. (11) Validation des dates schedule sur Maintenance : rejet explicite des Invalid Date au lieu de comparaisons NaN <= NaN silencieuses. (12) togglePanel admin : iteration sur childNodes pour trouver le textNode (l'icon child cassait `.firstChild.nodeValue`). TESTS : 136 tests v0.4.0 -> 159 tests v0.4.1 (+23 : URL protocol-relative, hex color, route hygiene, perf stress).

v0.4.0 - Systeme de themes visuels pour les annonces. 4 themes au choix : Velours et Or (le look actuel, defaut), OLED Total Black (fond noir pur monochrome avec JetBrains Mono, ideal ecrans OLED), Glow Neon (halo color rotatif selon importance avec Space Grotesk geometrique futuriste et pulse animation), Glassmorphism (fond tres flou translucide avec Manrope rond elegant, look macOS / Vision Pro). 4 polices web premium embarques (140 KB total : Inter, JetBrains Mono, Space Grotesk, Manrope) servies par le plugin sous /MaintenanceDeluxe/fonts/ avec cache immutable 1 an. v0.3.13 - Modal annonce centree + premium + templates rapides. (1) Fix critique de centrage : la modal apparaissait en haut a gauche en mode toast au lieu de centree plein ecran. Cause : un ancestor Jellyfin (body ou skinBody) avec transform/filter/will-change creait un containing block pour position:fixed, qui se rattachait a cet ancestor au lieu du viewport. Fix : CSS hardcode avec !important + 100vw/100vh explicites + append a document.documentElement (html) au lieu de body pour echapper a tout transform parent. (2) Style premium : backdrop blur passe a 8px, fond rgba(0,0,0,.68) plus contraste. (3) Templates rapides : 7 modeles pre-remplis dans l'admin pour ajouter une annonce en 1 clic au lieu de tout retaper (Mise a jour serveur, Nouveaux films, Maintenance prevue, Amelioration perfs avec comparisons, Annonce communautaire, Evenement, Alerte critique). Bouton dedie par modele dans la section Annonces. Bouton 'Nouvelle annonce' renomme '+ Annonce vide' pour clarifier l'alternative.

v0.3.12 - Fix critique : la modal d'annonce ne s'affichait pas apres login. Le hook fetchAndShowAnnouncements ne tournait qu'une seule fois au load initial de banner.js. Si l'user etait sur la page login (pas de token) au moment du chargement du script, le code exit early avant le hook annonces. Apres login - SPA navigate vers home - le hook n'etait jamais re-trigger. Fix : nouvelle fonction maybeShowAnnouncements() idempotente (track token deja checke) appelee dans refetchAndApplyMaintenance qui s'execute a chaque navigation SPA (hashchange / popstate / viewshow). Au passage de login (no-token -> token), le hook se declenche automatiquement avec un petit delay 800ms pour laisser la home page se mounter visuellement. Reset auto du flag au logout pour que la prochaine connexion re-trigger. Aucune autre regression - le init initial fonctionne identique pour les users deja loggues au chargement.

v0.3.11 - Fix critical : cache busting des assets admin apres upgrade plugin. Le user a constate apres l'install de v0.3.10 que l'UI admin restait identique a v0.3.9 (layout casse, pas de live preview) parce que le browser servait l'ancien admin.js/admin.css depuis son cache (Cache-Control: max-age=300 introduit en v0.3.4). Reecriture du helper ServeEmbeddedAsset : utilise maintenant ETag base sur la version d'assembly + Cache-Control 'public, no-cache, must-revalidate'. Au lieu de cacher 5 minutes en aveugle, le browser revalide a chaque navigation via If-None-Match - 304 Not Modified si la version n'a pas change (zero body, tres rapide), 200 avec nouveau code si upgrade plugin detecte. Cette classe de bug 'stale admin UI apres upgrade' qui frappait v0.3.4-v0.3.10 est definitivement fermee : a partir de v0.3.11, chaque release force un fetch frais des assets sans intervention de l'admin.

v0.3.10 - Refonte complete de l'editeur Annonces. Trois fix critiques sur la Phase 1 de v0.3.9 : (1) Le bouton Enregistrer global ne sauvait pas les annonces - il ignorait POST /announcements/admin. Maintenant les 3 saves (config, maintenance, announcements) tournent en parallele via Promise.allSettled avec rapport d'erreur unifie. (2) Layout desordonne : les champs et les comparaisons s'empilaient n'importe comment a cause d'un grid mal defini avec emby-input. Reecrit en grid CSS 2 colonnes (form gauche, preview right) avec fieldsets thematiques (Identite / Corps / Etat / Cible / Comparaisons / CTA) + sub-grids responsifs (mobile 1 col, desktop 2-3 cols). (3) Aucune previsualisation. Ajout d'un panneau live preview a droite de chaque editeur qui rend la modal d'annonce telle qu'elle apparaitra cote user, avec accent colorise selon l'importance + comparisons en mini-table + footer. Mise a jour en temps reel a chaque keystroke. Plus : bouton 'Enregistrer cette annonce' dedie par row avec badge dirty pulsant orange (au lieu de l'auto-save invisible et fragile). 174 lignes de CSS dedie ajoutees dans admin.css (jf-ann-* + pv-*).

Nouvelle fonctionnalite majeure : un systeme d'annonces dismissibles affichees aux utilisateurs apres login, idee pour pousser une mise a jour, un evenement, ou une release note enrichie. Chaque annonce a : titre + version + corps en markdown enrichi + icone + niveau d'importance (info/update/warning/critical avec accent colore distinct) + ciblage par role ET par UUID utilisateur specifique + comparaisons structurees avant/apres (Label/Before/After/Highlight) + bouton CTA optionnel. Modal client responsive : mobile portrait/paysage (stack comparisons), tablet, desktop (700px), TV (900px + font plus grand). Nouveaux endpoints : GET /announcements/active (any auth, retourne les non-vues filtrees par user), POST /{id}/seen (mark vu), GET /announcements/admin (full list + counts vu/total), POST /announcements/admin (save), POST /admin/{id}/reset-seen. 121 tests xUnit au total (89 + 32 nouveaux AnnouncementHelper). (1) Securite : GET /config retourne desormais un DTO BannerClientConfig sans webhook URL ni listes UUID (etait lisible par tout user authentifie) ; nouvel endpoint GET /config-admin (RequiresElevation) pour la page admin. v0.3.1 - Webhooks Discord/Slack + whitelist utilisateurs. (1) Notifications webhook : envoie un payload HTTP a chaque activation/desactivation de maintenance. Format Discord, Slack ou JSON generique auto-detecte depuis l'URL. Bouton 'Tester la notification' avec rate-limit 1 appel/5s par IP. URL HTTPS uniquement (pas de http://). Si le webhook est down, la maintenance s'active/se desactive quand meme - le webhook ne peut jamais bloquer le toggle. Doc payloads : docs/webhooks.md. (2) Liste blanche utilisateurs : nouveau widget multi-select dans la section Maintenance qui liste tous les utilisateurs Jellyfin. Les utilisateurs coches conservent leur acces pendant la maintenance (parfait pour la famille, l'astreinte, un compte de test). Les utilisateurs supprimes apparaissent en italique avec un bouton 'Retirer'. Edge case : un user ajoute apres l'activation reste desactive jusqu'au prochain toggle. (3) Privacy : l'endpoint public /MaintenanceDeluxe/maintenance ne renvoie plus les listes UUID (whitelist, disabled, pre-disabled) ni l'URL webhook - elles ne fuitent plus aux callers anonymes. Le admin UI passe par /config (auth) qui contient le state complet. (4) Backend : nouveau WebhookNotifier statique avec timeout 5s + 1 retry. Endpoint POST /maintenance/test-webhook et GET /users-summary, tous deux RequiresElevation.

v0.1.13 - UI FIX: gold card border was truncated when release notes made the overlay taller than the viewport. The card had its own internal scroll (max-height:92vh) so the ::before gold gradient didn't extend through scrolled content. Fix: overlay scrolls instead of card, card grows to full content height so the border wraps everything, and background layers (blobs, beams, grain, particles) are pinned to viewport with position:fixed.

v0.1.12 - CRITICAL FIX: Save button stopped reacting as soon as any field was modified. Root cause: a TypeError in collectMessages() aborted initDom before the Save handler got wired, because release-note rows shared the .jf-msg-row class with rotation messages and had no .jf-msg-detail. Fix: excluded .jf-rn-row from the rotation collector + defensive null guard in collectRowData.

v0.1.11 - CRITICAL FIX: admin config page was entirely unresponsive since v0.1.8. Root cause: release-note templates had real newlines inside JS string literals, causing the whole inline admin script to fail parsing. Every button, input, and save handler silently died. Now fixed — admin UI fully interactive again, tested with node --check.

v0.3.0 - Quality release: bug fixes + anti-data-loss + French admin UI. (1) Bugs: BannerController endpoints now return 503 if the plugin instance is not yet initialised instead of serving phantom defaults; ScheduledRestart is preserved when set after a maintenance window (only cleared if it was inside the window); MutationObserver and hideScrollObserver are now properly torn down on pagehide (no more memory leak after long sessions); live-preview postMessage receiver enforces same-origin checks (no cross-origin injection of overlay config). (2) Anti-data-loss: orange dot badge next to Save when there are unsaved changes, browser warning if you try to close the tab with unsaved changes, automatic localStorage draft autosaved every 500ms with restore prompt on next load, inline validation that flags scheduledEnd before scheduledStart and scheduledRestart in the past. (3) French admin UI: the Maintenance tab, Save button, save-confirmation modal, alerts and validations are fully translated to French. (4) The live-preview iframe now shows a clear fallback after a 5s timeout if the iframe never reports ready.

v0.2.3 - Two polish fixes on the new Appearance panel. First, the 'Agrandir l'apercu' button used Jellyfin's default emby-button which rendered with a white background on the dark admin theme; it now uses the same neutral-translucent style as the Reset button so it fits both light and dark themes. Second, new 'Rotatif' border option: a luminous gold gradient that slowly spins around the card, paired with a soft pulsing glow. Speed follows the animation scale slider (including the 'off' toggle).

v0.2.2 - Fine-tune beyond the presets. Every Animation speed and Particle density preset now has a companion numeric input (0-5× scale for animations, 0-500 for particle count). Click a preset to fill the number; type a number to override with any value in-range. Layout: appearance preview is now sticky (it follows you as you scroll the controls column), iframe min-height bumped to 540px so long release notes fit, controls column is tighter, expand-mode settings panel narrowed from 340px to 300px so the preview gets more room.

v0.2.1 - Polish on the new Appearance section: live preview iframe now loads correctly (the preview shell and banner.js endpoints no longer require Authorization headers that browsers don't send on iframe navigation, fixes 401 errors). The three enum selectors (animation speed, particle density, card border) are now segmented pill controls instead of plain radio buttons - much more readable and consistent with modern UI. Reset appearance button restyled so it is legible on both light and dark themes. Appearance labels, alerts and preview copy translated to French.

v0.2.0 - Appearance customization with live preview. New admin section lets you pick accent color, background tint, card opacity, animation speed (off/slow/normal/fast), particle density (none/low/normal/dense), and card border style (full gradient / simple gold / none). A live preview iframe reflects every change instantly without saving. Expand button gives a fullscreen view with toggleable settings panel (H hotkey) and Esc to exit. All colors are now derived from a single accent pick, so the palette stays coherent whatever hue you choose.

Added a visible warning on the website, when the plugin is disabled.

Added safety breaker / added better tooling in the configuration page.

A new feature has been added to the plugin: safety breaker. When the server serves traffic without the correct HTTP Header, it will trip (if the safety breaker is enabled) and disable the plugin. This is intended to catch misconfiguration that could result in people gaining access to the server.
Note that when the breaker trip, it will be visible in the configuration page.

Also, the configuration page now shows up which user is currently logged in with the header that was last saved, this should help with debugging.
Alternatively, if the javascript wasn't injected in the index.html page, it will display a corresponding message.

versions.changelog: v2.4.2 'Genre and studio badges that count what you watched' - FIXED (#154, thanks @mattsigal for his first PR, with once-per-item counting by @camarigor): TV episodes now credit studio badges with their series' studios (It's Not TV, Auntie Beeb and Netflix and Watch only ever saw movies); TMDb composite genres count for each part ('Action & Adventure' for Action Hero, 'Sci-Fi & Fantasy' for Sci-Fi Scholar and Fantasy Forever) and 'Sci-Fi' counts as 'Science Fiction'; studios match as a whole word plus aliases ('Walt Disney Pictures' counts for Disney, 'HBO Max' for HBO); every item counts once per badge however many of its names match. WHEN YOU UPDATE: watches already in your history start counting, so progress jumps and badges can unlock on the spot (on our server: 11 genre badges across 23 profiles, no progress went down); custom genre and studio badges match the same way (a custom 'War' badge now counts 'War & Politics'); episode plays from before this update stored no studio, so TV credit on studio badges starts now. FIXED (#147, @Roboatlas21, by @camarigor): the Friends chat's message box no longer sits behind a phone's navigation bar. CHANGED (#146, @Roboatlas21, by @camarigor): a plugin card image that survives the catalogue's crop. Deps: codeql-action 4.38.2, ClusterFuzzLite base image. 440/440 tests on both frameworks; smoke-tested on Jellyfin 10.11.10 and 12.1.0. Sigstore-signed + SLSA attested. Drop-in from v2.4.x - no migration.

v2.4.1 'What 2.4.0 got wrong, and a cap you can raise' - FIXED (#140, @Roboatlas21): the Jellyfin 12 package reported a version Jellyfin could not act on. Both assemblies were stamped x.y.z.0, so the dashboard showed 2.4.0.0 for an install the manifest called 2.4.0.1 - the plugin image 404'd and UNINSTALL FAILED OUTRIGHT. Each package now stamps the version it ships as. Stuck on 2.4.0.1? Updating through the catalogue is enough; the restart that loads the new build removes the old folder. FIXED (#141, @Roboatlas21): the page worked in a private window and nowhere else. A browser that cached Jellyfin's page before the plugin was installed revalidates it, Jellyfin answers 304 from the file on disk, and a 304 has no body to inject into - so the browser kept using a copy with no plugin in it. Worst where the web directory is read-only, since the on-disk patch cannot take either. The middleware now forces a full page while the patch has not taken. No need to clear browsing data; a normal reload is enough. CHANGED (#129, @Tschiyo): the targeted badge cap is a setting, 1 to 1000, default still 50, with the targets past it named on the page; the per-play check no longer grows with the target count (ancestor-set lookup, cached collection/playlist members). FIXED (#133, @clarjon1): the Revamp style reached the rest of Jellyfin - invisible checkboxes, text inputs losing border and height, selection colour changing everywhere, on Jellyfin's own controls and every other plugin's settings page. Twelve rules are now anchored to this plugin's own surfaces. FIXED (#131, @Borededdy): a Custom Tab rendered nothing under a theme that ships its own copy of Jellyfin's home page (Abyss); the plugin now builds the missing panel itself. NEW (#136, @Verdancy-Rin): a top-center toast placement plus an admin default for users who have not picked one; also fixed - the default UI style (#43) was never stored, and every main config save switched the page integrations back off. NEW (#138, @Digital-Yeti): optional, off by default - keep accounts hidden from Jellyfin's login screen out of other users' leaderboards, activity feed, friend search, compare picker and profile endpoints. FIXED: this plugin had been returning 500 for the whole server's /api-docs/openapi.json since 2.1.0 - its MediaType enum collided with Jellyfin's own type name and took the entire OpenAPI document down, breaking Swagger UI and every spec-driven client, silently. Renamed to BadgeMediaType; numbers and property names unchanged, nothing to migrate. 421/421 tests on both frameworks; verified live on Jellyfin 10.11.10 and 12.1.0. Sigstore-signed + SLSA attested. Drop-in from v2.4.0 - no schema change, no migration.

v2.4.0 'Jellyfin 12, targeted badges, games' - JELLYFIN 12 (#109): every release now ships two packages, x.y.z.0 for Jellyfin 10.11 (.NET 9) and x.y.z.1 for Jellyfin 12 (.NET 10); the catalog picks the right one. On 12 the Achievements entry is in the avatar menu below Profile, the equipped strip sits in the toolbar, every call sends the Authorization header 12 requires (legacy X-Emby-Token alone answers 401), the Revamp admin page fits the MUI dashboard, links use #/ routes. Thanks @camarigor (#117, #122, #128) and @Lyxon1337. NEW: targeted badges (#107) - ContainerCompletionPercent and ItemPlayCount point a badge at one series, season, collection, playlist, album or item via a library picker; retroactive on creation. NEW: JellyEmu game achievements (#115) - nine built-in badges and three custom metrics. NEW (#42): everything you equip in the shop - custom title, badge frame, profile theme, profile border, animated background, avatar - now shows on all three shareable-card skins and on the friends-drawer card. FIXED: toast placement under Revamp (#116); Pastel 'un-hidden elements' (every gradient theme let Jellyfin's page show through); profile borders never showed under Revamp; badge frames were nearly invisible on the achievements page; the shop's 'Auto-unlock at N score' pill was clipped; ~25 Users/Me requests on the login page; the Revamp stylesheet cached under a stale token in three places; admin hero reported v1.9.2 forever. #97 diagnostics: reset returns 400/404 for bad ids, admin errors name the failing request, an empty scan points at library access. 306/306 tests on both frameworks, smoke-tested on Jellyfin 12.0.0 and 10.11.10. Sigstore-signed + SLSA attested. Drop-in from v2.3.x.

versions.changelog:
# v2.6.4

A larger follow-up to v2.6.3 built almost entirely from contributor PRs: app passwords get safer and work for SSO and passkey accounts, admins can be alerted by email or Telegram, the setup page fits SSO-only users, and the dependency pins that held since the spring are finally lifted after live re-verification. Drop-in from any 2.5.x or 2.6.x, with no config or data migration.

## App passwords

- **An app password no longer signs in to the Jellyfin web interface** *(#249, by @camarigor; #244).* App passwords are for native apps; accepting one in a browser session defeats the point. A native client (Symfonium, Findroid, Seerr, and the like) still uses them exactly as before.
- **SSO and passkey accounts can create app passwords** *(#252/#248, by @camarigor).* Accounts that sign in through an identity provider or with a passkey, and so have no TOTP, were stuck with no way to make an app password for a native client. A linked provider (or a passkey) now satisfies the step-up that creating one requires.

## Sign-in and setup

- **Hide the plugin's 2FA setup from SSO users** *(#250/#247, by @camarigor).* An opt-in admin setting: a non-admin who signs in through a linked provider sees that the provider handles sign-in instead of the plugin's own TOTP/passkey enrolment. Administrators keep the full page.
- **A clearer authenticator rotation flow** *(#255/#254, by @camarigor).* The setup page shows the rotate card, and your old authenticator keeps working until the new one is confirmed.
- **OIDC errors tell a refused sign-in apart from an expired code** *(#234/#64, by @camarigor).*
- **The login page works behind an access proxy** *(#253/#251, by @camarigor):* the plugin's own requests now carry the page's cookies.
- **The admin Users tab saves an edited email reliably** through the step-up prompt *(#264/#263, by @camarigor).*

## Notifications and detection

- **Admin alert emails, and Telegram as a channel** *(#261/#259, by @camarigor).* Security events (suspicious sign-in, emergency lockout) can now notify admins by email or Telegram.
- **Turn suspicious-login detection off** *(#260/#258, by @camarigor),* and leave impossible-travel out of the security score when geo checks run elsewhere.

## Correctness

- **Sign-in no longer saves a stale copy of the user record** *(#257/#256, by @camarigor),* which could drop a concurrent change made during sign-in.

## Dependencies

- **The QuestPDF and IdentityModel pins are lifted** *(#262, by @camarigor).* `Microsoft.IdentityModel.Tokens` / `System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt` move to 8.23.0 and QuestPDF to 2026.9.1, after re-verifying a live OIDC sign-in and the recovery-code PDF on both the 10.11 and 12 builds. The spring OIDC regression turned out to be a missing bundled assembly, shipped since v2.6.2, not the library. Fido2 moves to 4.2.0 and MailKit to 4.18.1. The Jellyfin runtime references stay pinned.

## Upgrade notes

In-place upgrade from any 2.5.x or 2.6.x, with no schema or configuration migration. Both the 10.11 (.NET 9) and 12 (.NET 10) packages are published and your server selects the right one automatically. Sigstore-signed and SLSA build-provenance attested.

# v2.6.3

A safety release on top of v2.6.2: uninstalling, disabling, or losing the plugin no longer locks out the accounts that used it. Drop-in from any 2.5.x or 2.6.x, with no config or data migration.

## Accounts are handed back to Jellyfin when the plugin goes away

*(Fixes #232, seen in #213, by @camarigor.)*

Signing in with a passkey, creating an app password, or using the OIDC bridge moves an account onto the plugin's own sign-in provider, and nothing moved it back. So once the plugin was uninstalled, disabled, or failed to load, Jellyfin refused every sign-in for those accounts, administrators included.

The plugin now hands those accounts back to Jellyfin's own authentication provider when it is uninstalled or disabled, and takes them back the next time it starts (so an app password created before the uninstall works again after a reinstall). Concretely:

- **Uninstall** moves every account on the plugin's provider back to the provider the plugin was delegating password checks to (Jellyfin's default on a stock server), before Jellyfin removes the plugin.
- **Disable** does the same, through a filter that runs after Jellyfin disables the plugin.
- **Reinstall / re-enable** then restores those accounts to the plugin on the next start, each only while it is still on the handed-back provider.

The hand-back only ever runs on an administrator's own uninstall or disable, and only moves accounts that are actually on the plugin's provider; while the plugin is running, nothing changes.

## Recovery when the plugin cannot load

No code can run for a plugin folder that was deleted or a build that will not load, so the README now documents the ways out: re-enable and restart, save the account's profile page (which moves it to the default provider), or the two-line `sqlite3` fix with Jellyfin stopped.

## Upgrade notes

In-place upgrade from any 2.5.x or 2.6.x, with no schema or configuration migration. The only new on-disk state is a short-lived `handed-back.json` that exists between a hand-back and the next start. Both the 10.11 (.NET 9) and 12 (.NET 10) packages are published and your server selects the right one automatically. Sigstore-signed and SLSA build-provenance attested.

# v2.6.1

A focused fix release on top of v2.6.0: OIDC sign-in now hands off to the 2FA prompt correctly when a user has both SSO and plugin TOTP, and a native-library crash that could core-dump the whole Jellyfin process is gone. Drop-in from any 2.5.x or 2.6.0, with no config or data migration.

## OIDC sign-in reaches the 2FA prompt instead of erroring

*(Fixes #204, by @Faffu.)*

If a user signed in with OIDC/SSO **and** also had plugin TOTP enabled, the sign-in stopped on the callback page with **"Sign-in could not be completed. Error: HTTP 401"**. That 401 was actually the expected `TwoFactorRequired` response with a challenge token, but the bridge page treated any 401 as a terminal failure and never opened the TOTP page.

Both sign-in bridges (the browser callback and the in-app webview) now recognise a `TwoFactorRequired` response and continue to the existing 2FA challenge, then complete sign-in once the code is accepted. A wrong code is still rejected, an ordinary 401 is still an authentication failure, and credentials are not stored before the second factor is completed. The challenge redirect is built from the server's own base path, never from anything in the response.

## No more `libsodium` core dumps

*(Fixes #203, reported by @bluej007.)*

On some hosts (seen on the linuxserver.io image on Jellyfin 12) the Jellyfin process could randomly core-dump while browsing the dashboard, with the crash inside the dynamic linker loading `libsodium.so`.

The cause was the recovery-code PDF service eagerly loading `libsodium.so` as if it were a QuestPDF dependency. It is not: `libsodium` belongs to the passkey code (NSec), and loading it late from the PDF path meant even servers that never use passkeys pulled it in, where a late load of that library can crash glibc's loader outright. The PDF service now loads only its real native dependencies; `libsodium` is loaded on demand only when a passkey is actually used, so passkeys are unaffected and everyone else stops crashing.

## Upgrade notes

In-place upgrade from any 2.5.x or 2.6.0, with no schema or configuration migration. Both the 10.11 (.NET 9) and 12 (.NET 10) packages are published for this version and your server selects the right one automatically. Sigstore-signed and SLSA build-provenance attested.

# v2.6.0

**Jellyfin 12 is supported.** This release ships a second build so the plugin loads and runs on Jellyfin 12 (which moved to .NET 10), while the existing build keeps serving Jellyfin 10.11.x exactly as before. Both live in the one plugin catalog under the same entry, so your server downloads the build that matches its version: there is nothing to pick and existing installs update themselves. It also fixes the admin step-up prompt on the settings save path and the OIDC provider form, and makes the GeoIP diagnostics finally explain themselves. Drop-in from any 2.5.x, with no config or data migration.

## Jellyfin 12 support, without dropping 10.11

*(Closes #196 and #172.)*

Jellyfin 12 moved to .NET 10, and a plugin compiled against 10.11 (.NET 9) will not load on it, which is why every action returned **401 / "Unauthorized"** on 12 (#172). Rather than fork the plugin or abandon 10.11 users, this release builds the **same source twice**:

- a **.NET 9** build for Jellyfin **10.11.x** hosts, and
- a **.NET 10** build for Jellyfin **12.x** hosts.

Both are published in the one `manifest.json` under the same plugin, keyed by the Jellyfin version each needs. Jellyfin's own catalog keeps the builds whose target version is at or below your server's and installs the newest, so a 12 server pulls the .NET 10 build, a 10.11 server pulls the .NET 9 build, and neither ever sees the other. **You do not choose a download**: the catalog and auto-update do it for you. If you install manually from the Releases page instead, grab the `-jf12` zip on Jellyfin 12 and the plain zip on 10.11.

Everything was verified end to end on a real Jellyfin 12 server and a Jellyfin 10.11 server: sign-in, refresh persistence, OIDC/SSO, TOTP, email OTP, recovery codes, passkeys, app passwords, admin step-up, the PDF recovery-code export, and the admin dashboard page.

**Related 12 fixes rolled in:**

- **#191** *(camarigor)*: in-app OIDC sign-in on 12 froze on a blank screen. On 12 the router asks for the server connection before the reconnect that 10.11 did first, so the stored credential (which had no resolvable address) left the client pointing at nothing. The sign-in bridge now stores the address it just authenticated against, in the connection mode 12 expects.
- **#193** *(camarigor)*: 12 changed some web routes, so the plugin's setup link and the way it re-enters the setup page needed updating. 12 users get a working way back to the setup page from the avatar menu.
- Completes the header work from v2.5.22 (#174/#180): the plugin's pages and endpoints accept Jellyfin's current `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token` header, which 12 requires once legacy authorization is disabled.

## The admin step-up prompt now appears everywhere it should

*(Closes #198 and #194; helps #189 and #148.)*

The server has gated the sensitive admin actions (creating, editing and deleting OIDC providers, toggling a user's 2FA, "require password setup", and reading the audit log) behind a **step-up** re-authentication since v2.5.6. But some of the admin page's own calls sent those requests with a plain `fetch`, so the server's `403 { stepUpRequired: true }` came back as a bare **"Save failed"** and, for provider **Delete**, nothing happened at all (#198). Adding an identity provider on a step-up-protected server was simply impossible.

- **#198 / #199** *(camarigor)*: the provider form and the shared admin helpers now go through the step-up-aware fetch that Save Settings has used since v2.5.8. When step-up is required you get the prompt; when something else fails you get the server's actual reason instead of a generic message.
- **#194 / #195** *(camarigor)*: the admin step-up modal previously accepted only a typed TOTP code, locking out admins whose second factor is an **emailed code** or a **passkey**. It now offers the emailed code and a passkey alongside TOTP, using the same unified proof the rest of the plugin uses.

If you hit "valid code rejected at step-up" on 10.11 (#189), please retest on this build: the step-up verification and the admin-call routing both changed here.

## GeoIP diagnostics that explain themselves

*(#200, camarigor. Refs #51.)*

Three people reported `GeoIP databases loaded = Fail` with the files in place, and none had a log line to go on, because the loader had nothing to say: it fixed the configured path before trying to open it, a file the process could not see was skipped in silence, and a failed load was never retried until the path changed or Jellyfin restarted. Now the loader keeps the reason, retries, and falls back to an in-memory open, and the Diagnostics tab prints what it saw for **each** database. A bad path no longer reads as a blank "Fail": it says, for example, `not found at /config/geoip/GeoLite2-ASN.mmdb (its directory is not visible to the Jellyfin process; checked as user root)` or `rejected (not absolute)`, so you can actually fix it.

## Upgrade notes

In-place upgrade from any 2.5.x, with no schema or configuration migration. 500 tests pass. Sigstore-signed and SLSA build-provenance attested. Both the 10.11 (.NET 9) and 12 (.NET 10) packages are published for this version; your server selects the right one automatically.

name: Missing Episodes [✓]
description:
Scan your Jellyfin library, Sonarr, or TMDB for missing TV episodes and send them to Sonarr.
